scenes.title: Where might sing the sweet-voiced cuckoo,

scenes.title: Through the air he came a-flying,

scenes.reentry: That he might this thing consider; And he spake the words that follow: “Wherefore, ancient Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: That the birds may nest within it,
scenes.place: That the birds may nest within it,

scenes.title: Spake the eagle, thus replying:
scenes.place: Spake the eagle, thus replying:
scenes.reentry: “Good indeed, thy hero-judgment, That the birch-tree thou hast left us,

scenes.title: Left the sacred birch-tree standing,
scenes.place: Left the sacred birch-tree standing,
scenes.reentry: As a resting-place for eagles, And for birds of every feather,

scenes.title: Even I may rest upon it.”
scenes.place: Even I may rest upon it.”
scenes.reentry: Quickly then this bird of heaven, Kindled fire among the branches;

scenes.title: Soon the flames are fanned by north-winds,
scenes.place: Soon the flames are fanned by north-winds,
scenes.reentry: And the east-winds lend their forces, Burn the trees of all descriptions,

scenes.title: Burn them all to dust and ashes,
scenes.place: Burn them all to dust and ashes,
scenes.reentry: Only is the birch left standing.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, wise and ancient,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, wise and ancient,

scenes.place: Brings them from his trusty pouches,
scenes.reentry: Fashioned from the skin of squirrel, Some were made from skin of marten.

scenes.title: Thence to sow his seeds he hastens,
scenes.place: Thence to sow his seeds he hastens,
scenes.reentry: Hastes the barley-grains to scatter, Speaks unto himself these measures: “I the seeds of life am sowing,

scenes.title: Sowing through my open fingers,
scenes.place: Sowing through my open fingers,
scenes.reentry: From the hand of my Creator, In this soil enriched with ashes,

scenes.title: In this soil to sprout and flourish
scenes.place: In this soil to sprout and flourish
scenes.reentry: Ancient mother, thou that livest Far below the earth and ocean,

scenes.title: Mother of the fields and forests,
scenes.place: Mother of the fields and forests,
scenes.reentry: Bring the rich soil to producing, Bring the seed-grains to the sprouting,

scenes.title: That the barley well may flourish
scenes.place: That the barley well may flourish
scenes.reentry: Never will the earth unaided, Yield the ripe nutritious barley;

scenes.title: Never will her force be wanting,
scenes.place: Never will her force be wanting,
scenes.reentry: If the givers give assistance, If the givers grace the sowing,

scenes.title: Grace the daughters of creation
scenes.place: Grace the daughters of creation
scenes.reentry: Rise, O earth, from out thy slumber, From the slumber-land of ages,

scenes.title: Let the barley-grains be sprouting,
scenes.place: Let the barley-grains be sprouting,
scenes.reentry: Let the blades themselves be starting, Let the verdant stalks be rising,

scenes.title: Let the ears themselves be growing,
scenes.place: Let the ears themselves be growing,
scenes.reentry: And a hundredfold producing, From my plowing and my sowing,

scenes.title: From my skilled and honest labor
scenes.place: From my skilled and honest labor
scenes.reentry: Ukko, thou O God, up yonder, Thou O Father of the heavens,

scenes.title: Thou that livest high in Ether,
scenes.place: Thou that livest high in Ether,
scenes.reentry: Curbest all the clouds of heaven, Holdest in the air thy counsel,

scenes.title: Holdest in the clouds good counsel,
scenes.place: Holdest in the clouds good counsel,
scenes.reentry: From the East dispatch a cloudlet, From the North-east send a rain-cloud,

scenes.title: From the West another send us,
scenes.place: From the West another send us,
scenes.reentry: From the North-west, still another, Quickly from the South a warm-cloud,

scenes.title: That the rain may fall from heaven,
scenes.place: That the rain may fall from heaven,
scenes.reentry: That the clouds may drop their honey, That the ears may fill and ripen,

scenes.title: That the barley-fields may rustle.”
scenes.place: That the barley-fields may rustle.”
scenes.reentry: Thereupon benignant Ukko,

scenes.title: Ukko, father of the heavens,
scenes.place: Ukko, father of the heavens,
scenes.reentry: Held his counsel in the cloud-space, Held good counsel in the Ether;

scenes.title: From the East, he sent a cloudlet,
scenes.place: From the East, he sent a cloudlet,
scenes.reentry: From the North-east, sent a rain-cloud, From the West another sent he,

scenes.title: From the North-west, still another,
scenes.place: From the North-west, still another,
scenes.reentry: Quickly from the South a warm-cloud; Joined in seams the clouds together,

scenes.title: Sewed together all their edges,
scenes.place: Sewed together all their edges,
scenes.reentry: Grasped the cloud, and hurled it earthward. Quick the rain-cloud drops her honey,

scenes.title: Quick the rain-drops fall from heaven,
scenes.place: Quick the rain-drops fall from heaven,
scenes.reentry: That the ears may quickly ripen, That the barley crop may rustle.

scenes.title: Straightway grow the seeds of barley,
scenes.place: Straightway grow the seeds of barley,
scenes.reentry: From the germ the blade unfolding, Richly colored ears arising,

scenes.title: From the rich soil of the fallow,
scenes.place: From the rich soil of the fallow,
scenes.reentry: From the work of Wainamoinen.

scenes.title: Here a few days pass unnoted
scenes.place: Here a few days pass unnoted
scenes.reentry: And as many nights fly over. When the seventh day had journeyed,

scenes.title: On the morning of the eighth day,
scenes.place: On the morning of the eighth day,
scenes.reentry: Wainamoinen, wise and ancient, Went to view his crop of barley,

scenes.title: How his plowing, how his sowing,
scenes.place: How his plowing, how his sowing,
scenes.reentry: How his labors were resulting; Found his crop of barley growing,

scenes.title: Found the blades were triple-knotted,
scenes.place: Found the blades were triple-knotted,
scenes.reentry: And the ears he found six-sided.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, old and trusty,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, old and trusty,
scenes.reentry: Turned his face, and looked about him, Lo! there comes a spring-time cuckoo,

scenes.title: Spying out the slender birch-tree,
scenes.place: Spying out the slender birch-tree,
scenes.reentry: Rests upon it, sweetly singing: “Wherefore is the silver birch-tree

scenes.title: Left unharmed of all the forest?”
scenes.place: Left unharmed of all the forest?”
scenes.reentry: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen: “Therefore I have left the birch-tree,

scenes.title: Left the birch-tree only growing,
scenes.place: Left the birch-tree only growing,
scenes.reentry: Home for thee for joyful singing. Call thou here, O sweet-voiced cuckoo,

scenes.title: Sing thou here from throat of velvet,
scenes.place: Sing thou here from throat of velvet,
scenes.reentry: Sing thou here with voice of silver, Sing the cuckoo’s golden flute-notes;

scenes.title: Call at morning, call at evening,
scenes.place: Call at morning, call at evening,
scenes.reentry: Call within the hour of noontide, For the better growth of forests,

scenes.title: For the ripening of the barley,
scenes.place: For the ripening of the barley,
scenes.reentry: For the richness of, the Northland, For the joy of Kalevala.”

scenes.title: Rune Iii
scenes.place: Rune Iii
scenes.reentry: Wainamoinen and Youkahainen.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, ancient minstrel,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, ancient minstrel,
scenes.reentry: Passed his years in full contentment, On the meadows of Wainola,

scenes.title: On the plains of Kalevala,
scenes.place: On the plains of Kalevala,
scenes.reentry: Singing ever wondrous legends, Songs of ancient wit and wisdom,

scenes.title: Chanting one day, then a second,
scenes.place: Chanting one day, then a second,
scenes.reentry: Singing in the dusk of evening, Singing till the dawn of morning,

scenes.title: Now the tales of old-time heroes,
scenes.place: Now the tales of old-time heroes,
scenes.reentry: Tales of ages long forgotten, Now the legends of creation,

scenes.title: Once familiar to the children,
scenes.place: Once familiar to the children,
scenes.reentry: By our children sung no longer, Sung in part by many heroes,

scenes.title: In these mournful days of evil,
scenes.place: In these mournful days of evil,
scenes.reentry: Evil days our race befallen. Far and wide the story travelled,

scenes.title: Far away men spread the knowledge
scenes.place: Far away men spread the knowledge
scenes.reentry: Of the chanting of the hero, Of the song of Wainamoinen;

scenes.title: To the South were heard the echoes,
scenes.place: To the South were heard the echoes,
scenes.reentry: All of Northland heard the story.

scenes.title: Far away in dismal Northland,
scenes.place: Far away in dismal Northland,
scenes.reentry: Lived the singer, Youkahainen, Lapland’s young and reckless minstrel.

scenes.title: Once upon a time when feasting,
scenes.place: Once upon a time when feasting,
scenes.reentry: Dining with his friends and fellows, Came upon his ears the story,

scenes.title: That there lived a sweeter singer,
scenes.place: That there lived a sweeter singer,
scenes.reentry: On the meadows of Wainola, On the plains of Kalevala,

scenes.title: Better skilled in chanting legends,
scenes.place: Better skilled in chanting legends,
scenes.reentry: Better skilled than Youkahainen, Better than the one that taught him.

scenes.title: Straightway then the bard grew angry,
scenes.place: Straightway then the bard grew angry,
scenes.reentry: Envy rose within his bosom, Envy of this Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Famed to be a sweeter singer;
scenes.place: Famed to be a sweeter singer;
scenes.reentry: Hastes he angry to his mother, To his mother, full of wisdom,

scenes.title: Vows that he will southward hasten,
scenes.place: Vows that he will southward hasten,
scenes.reentry: Hie him southward and betake him To the dwellings of Wainola,

scenes.title: To the cabins of the Northland,
scenes.place: To the cabins of the Northland,
scenes.reentry: There as bard to vie in battle, With the famous Wainamoinen.

scenes.title: There with him to offer battle;
scenes.place: There with him to offer battle;
scenes.reentry: He will charm thee with his singing Will bewitch thee in his anger,

scenes.title: He will drive thee back dishonored,
scenes.place: He will drive thee back dishonored,
scenes.reentry: Sink thee in the fatal snow-drift, Turn to ice thy pliant fingers,

scenes.title: Turn to ice thy feet and ankles.”
scenes.place: Turn to ice thy feet and ankles.”
scenes.reentry: These the words of Youkahainen: “Good the judgement of a father,

scenes.title: Better still, a mother’s counsel,
scenes.place: Better still, a mother’s counsel,
scenes.reentry: Best of all one’s own decision. I will go and face the minstrel,

scenes.title: Challenge him to sing in contest,
scenes.place: Challenge him to sing in contest,
scenes.reentry: Challenge him as bard to battle, Sing to him my sweet-toned measures,

scenes.title: Chant to him my oldest legends,
scenes.place: Chant to him my oldest legends,
scenes.reentry: Chant to him my garnered wisdom, That this best of boasted singers,

scenes.title: That this famous bard of Suomi,
scenes.place: That this famous bard of Suomi,
scenes.reentry: Shall be worsted in the contest, Shall become a hapless minstrel;

scenes.title: By my songs shall I transform him,
scenes.place: By my songs shall I transform him,
scenes.reentry: That his feet shall be as flint-stone, And as oak his nether raiment;

scenes.title: And this famous, best of singers,
scenes.place: And this famous, best of singers,
scenes.reentry: Thus bewitched, shall carry ever, In his heart a stony burden,

scenes.title: On his shoulder bow of marble,
scenes.place: On his shoulder bow of marble,
scenes.reentry: On his hand a flint-stone gauntlet, On his brow a stony visor.”

scenes.title: Then the wizard, Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Then the wizard, Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Heeding not advice paternal, Heeding not his mother’s counsel,

scenes.title: Leads his courser from his stable,
scenes.place: Leads his courser from his stable,
scenes.reentry: Fire outstreaming from his nostrils, From his hoofs, the sparks outshooting,

scenes.title: Hitches to his sledge, the fleet-foot,
scenes.place: Hitches to his sledge, the fleet-foot,
scenes.reentry: To his golden sledge, the courser, Mounts impetuous his snow-sledge,

scenes.title: Leaps upon the hindmost cross-bench,
scenes.place: Leaps upon the hindmost cross-bench,
scenes.reentry: Strikes his courser with his birch-whip, With his birch-whip, pearl-enamelled.

scenes.title: Instantly the prancing racer
scenes.place: Instantly the prancing racer
scenes.reentry: Springs away upon his journey; On he, restless, plunges northward,

scenes.title: All day long he onward gallops,
scenes.place: All day long he onward gallops,
scenes.reentry: All the next day, onward, onward, So the third from morn till evening,

scenes.title: Till the third day twilight brings him
scenes.place: Till the third day twilight brings him
scenes.reentry: To the meadows of Wainola, To the plains of Kalevala.

scenes.title: As it happened, Wainamoinen,
scenes.place: As it happened, Wainamoinen,
scenes.reentry: Wainamoinen, the magician, Rode that sunset on the highway,

scenes.title: Silently for pleasure driving
scenes.place: Silently for pleasure driving
scenes.reentry: Down Wainola’s peaceful meadows, O’er the plains of Kalevala.

scenes.title: Youkahainen, young and fiery,
scenes.place: Youkahainen, young and fiery,
scenes.reentry: Urging still his foaming courser, Dashes down upon the singer,

scenes.title: Does not turn aside in meeting,
scenes.place: Does not turn aside in meeting,
scenes.reentry: Meeting thus in full collision; Shafts are driven tight together,

scenes.title: Hames and collars wedged and tangled,
scenes.place: Hames and collars wedged and tangled,
scenes.reentry: Tangled are the reins and traces. Thus perforce they make a stand-still,

scenes.title: Thus remain and well consider;
scenes.place: Thus remain and well consider;
scenes.reentry: Water drips from hame and collar, Vapors rise from both their horses.

scenes.title: Speaks the minstrel, Wainamoinen:
scenes.place: Speaks the minstrel, Wainamoinen:
scenes.reentry: “Who art thou, and whence? Thou comest Driving like a stupid stripling,

scenes.title: Careless, dashing down upon me
scenes.place: Careless, dashing down upon me
scenes.reentry: Thou hast ruined shafts and traces; And the collar of my racer

scenes.title: Thou hast shattered into ruin,
scenes.place: Thou hast shattered into ruin,
scenes.reentry: And my golden sleigh is broken, Box and runners dashed to pieces.”

scenes.title: Youkahainen then make answer,
scenes.place: Youkahainen then make answer,
scenes.reentry: Spake at last the words that follow: “I am youthful Youkahainen,

scenes.title: But make answer first, who thou art,
scenes.place: But make answer first, who thou art,
scenes.reentry: Whence thou comest, where thou goest, From what lowly tribe descended?”

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, wise and ancient,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, wise and ancient,
scenes.reentry: Answered thus the youthful minstrel: “If thou art but Youkahainen,

scenes.title: Thou shouldst give me all the highway;
scenes.place: Thou shouldst give me all the highway;
scenes.reentry: I am many years thy senior.”

scenes.title: Then the boastful Youkahainen
scenes.place: Then the boastful Youkahainen
scenes.reentry: Spake again to Wainamoinen: “Young or ancient, little matter,

scenes.title: Little consequence the age is;
scenes.place: Little consequence the age is;
scenes.reentry: He that higher stands in wisdom, He whose knowledge is the greater,

scenes.title: He that is the sweeter singer,
scenes.place: He that is the sweeter singer,
scenes.reentry: He alone shall keep the highway, And the other take the roadside.

scenes.title: Art thou ancient Wainamoinen,
scenes.place: Art thou ancient Wainamoinen,
scenes.reentry: Famous sorcerer and minstrel? Let us then begin our singing,

scenes.title: Let us sing our ancient legends,
scenes.place: Let us sing our ancient legends,
scenes.reentry: Let us chant our garnered wisdom, That the one may hear the other,

scenes.title: That the one may judge the other,
scenes.place: That the one may judge the other,
scenes.reentry: In a war of wizard sayings.”

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, wise and ancient,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, wise and ancient,
scenes.reentry: Thus replied in modest accents: “What I know is very little,

scenes.title: Hardly is it worth the singing,
scenes.place: Hardly is it worth the singing,
scenes.reentry: Neither is my singing wondrous: All my days I have resided

scenes.title: In the cold and dreary Northland,
scenes.place: In the cold and dreary Northland,
scenes.reentry: In a desert land enchanted, In my cottage home for ages;

scenes.title: All the songs that I have gathered,
scenes.place: All the songs that I have gathered,
scenes.reentry: Are the cuckoo’s simple measures, Some of these I may remember;

scenes.title: But since thou perforce demandest,
scenes.place: But since thou perforce demandest,
scenes.reentry: I accept thy boastful challenge. Tell me now, my golden youngster,

scenes.title: What thou knowest more than others,
scenes.place: What thou knowest more than others,
scenes.reentry: Open now thy store of wisdom.”

scenes.title: Thus made answer Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Thus made answer Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Lapland’s young and fiery minstrel: “Know I many bits of learning,

scenes.title: This I know in perfect clearness:
scenes.place: This I know in perfect clearness:
scenes.reentry: Every roof must have a chimney, Every fire-place have a hearth-stone;

scenes.title: Lives of seal are free and merry,
scenes.place: Lives of seal are free and merry,
scenes.reentry: Merry is the life of walrus, Feeding on incautious salmon,

scenes.title: Daily eating perch and whiting;
scenes.place: Daily eating perch and whiting;
scenes.reentry: Whitings live in quiet shallows, Salmon love the level bottoms;

scenes.title: Spawns the pike in coldest weather,
scenes.place: Spawns the pike in coldest weather,
scenes.reentry: And defies the storms of winter. Slowly perches swim in Autumn,

scenes.title: Wry-backed, hunting deeper water,
scenes.place: Wry-backed, hunting deeper water,
scenes.reentry: Spawn in shallows in the summer, Bounding on the shore of ocean.

scenes.title: Should this wisdom seem too little,
scenes.place: Should this wisdom seem too little,
scenes.reentry: I can tell thee other matters, Sing thee other wizard sayings:

scenes.title: All the Northmen plow with reindeer,
scenes.place: All the Northmen plow with reindeer,
scenes.reentry: Mother-horses plow the Southland, Inner Lapland plows with oxen;

scenes.title: All the trees on Pisa-mountain,
scenes.place: All the trees on Pisa-mountain,
scenes.reentry: Know I well in all their grandeur; On the Horna-rock are fir-trees,

scenes.title: Fir-trees growing tall and slender;
scenes.place: Fir-trees growing tall and slender;
scenes.reentry: Slender grow the trees on mountains. Three, the water-falls in number,

scenes.title: Three in number, inland oceans,
scenes.place: Three in number, inland oceans,
scenes.reentry: Three in number, lofty mountains, Shooting to the vault of heaven.

scenes.title: Hallapyora’s near to Yaemen,
scenes.place: Hallapyora’s near to Yaemen,
scenes.reentry: Katrakoski in Karyala; Imatra, the falling water,

scenes.title: Tumbles, roaring, into Wuoksi.”
scenes.place: Tumbles, roaring, into Wuoksi.”
scenes.reentry: Then the ancient Wainamoinen: “Women’s tales and children’s wisdom

scenes.title: Do not please a bearded hero,
scenes.place: Do not please a bearded hero,
scenes.reentry: Hero, old enough for wedlock; Tell the story of creation,

scenes.title: Tell me of the world’s beginning,
scenes.place: Tell me of the world’s beginning,
scenes.reentry: Tell me of the creatures in it, And philosophize a little.”

scenes.title: Then the youthful Youkahainen
scenes.place: Then the youthful Youkahainen
scenes.reentry: Thus replied to Wainamoinen: “Know I well the titmouse-fountains,

scenes.title: Pretty birdling is the titmouse;
scenes.place: Pretty birdling is the titmouse;
scenes.reentry: And the viper, green, a serpent; Whitings live in brackish waters;

scenes.title: Perches swim in every river;
scenes.place: Perches swim in every river;
scenes.reentry: Iron rusts, and rusting weakens; Bitter is the taste of umber;

scenes.title: Boiling water is malicious;
scenes.place: Boiling water is malicious;
scenes.reentry: Fire is ever full of danger; First physician, the Creator;

scenes.title: Remedy the oldest, water;
scenes.place: Remedy the oldest, water;
scenes.reentry: Magic is the child of sea-foam; God the first and best adviser;

scenes.title: Waters gush from every mountain;
scenes.place: Waters gush from every mountain;
scenes.reentry: Fire descended first from heaven; Iron from the rust was fashioned;

scenes.title: Copper from the rocks created;
scenes.place: Copper from the rocks created;
scenes.reentry: Marshes are of lands the oldest; First of all the trees, the willow;

scenes.title: Fir-trees were the first of houses;
scenes.place: Fir-trees were the first of houses;
scenes.reentry: Hollowed stones the first of kettles.”

scenes.title: Now the ancient Wainamoinen
scenes.place: Now the ancient Wainamoinen
scenes.reentry: Thus addresses Youkahainen: “Canst thou give me now some wisdom,

scenes.title: Is this nonsense all thou knowest?”
scenes.place: Is this nonsense all thou knowest?”
scenes.reentry: Youkahainen thus made answer: “I can tell thee still a trifle,

scenes.title: Tell thee of the times primeval,
scenes.place: Tell thee of the times primeval,
scenes.reentry: When I plowed the salt-sea’s bosom, When I raked the sea-girt islands,

scenes.title: When I dug the salmon-grottoes,
scenes.place: When I dug the salmon-grottoes,
scenes.reentry: Hollowed out the deepest caverns, When I all the lakes created,

scenes.title: When I heaped the mountains round them,
scenes.place: When I heaped the mountains round them,
scenes.reentry: When I piled the rocks about them. I was present as a hero,

scenes.title: Sixth of wise and ancient heroes,
scenes.place: Sixth of wise and ancient heroes,
scenes.reentry: Seventh of all primeval heroes, When the heavens were created,

scenes.title: When were formed the ether-spaces,
scenes.place: When were formed the ether-spaces,
scenes.reentry: When the sky was crystal-pillared, When was arched the beauteous rainbow,

scenes.title: When the Moon was placed in orbit,
scenes.place: When the Moon was placed in orbit,
scenes.reentry: When the silver Sun was planted, When the Bear was firmly stationed,

scenes.title: And with stars the heavens were sprinkled.”
scenes.place: And with stars the heavens were sprinkled.”
scenes.reentry: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen: “Thou art surely prince of liars,

scenes.title: Lord of all the host of liars;
scenes.place: Lord of all the host of liars;
scenes.reentry: Never wert thou in existence, Surely wert thou never present,

scenes.title: When was plowed the salt-sea’s bosom,
scenes.place: When was plowed the salt-sea’s bosom,
scenes.reentry: When were raked the sea-girt islands, When were dug the salmon-grottoes,

scenes.title: When were hollowed out the caverns,
scenes.place: When were hollowed out the caverns,
scenes.reentry: When the lakes were all created, When were heaped the mountains round them,

scenes.title: When the rocks were piled about them
scenes.place: When the rocks were piled about them
scenes.reentry: Thou wert never seen or heard of When the earth was first created,

scenes.title: When were made the ether-spaces,
scenes.place: When were made the ether-spaces,
scenes.reentry: When the air was crystal-pillared, When the Moon was placed in orbit,

scenes.title: When the silver Sun was planted,
scenes.place: When the silver Sun was planted,
scenes.reentry: When the Bear was firmly stationed, When the skies with stars were sprinkled.”

scenes.title: Then in anger Youkahainen
scenes.place: Then in anger Youkahainen
scenes.reentry: Answered ancient Wainamoinen: “Then, sir, since I fail in wisdom,

scenes.title: With the sword I offer battle;
scenes.place: With the sword I offer battle;
scenes.reentry: Come thou, famous bard and minstrel, Thou the ancient wonder-singer,

scenes.title: Let us try our strength with broadswords,
scenes.place: Let us try our strength with broadswords,
scenes.reentry: Let our blades be fully tested.” Spake the ancient Wainamoinen: “Not thy sword and not thy wisdom,

scenes.title: Not thy prudence, nor thy cunning,
scenes.place: Not thy prudence, nor thy cunning,
scenes.reentry: Do I fear a single moment. Let who may accept thy challenge,

scenes.title: Not with thee, a puny braggart,
scenes.place: Not with thee, a puny braggart,
scenes.reentry: Not with one so vain and paltry, Will I ever measure broadswords.”

scenes.title: Then the youthful Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Then the youthful Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Mouth awry and visage sneering, Shook his golden locks and answered: “Whoso fears his blade to measure,

scenes.title: Fears to test his strength at broadswords,
scenes.place: Fears to test his strength at broadswords,
scenes.reentry: Into wild-boar of the forest, Swine at heart and swine in visage,

scenes.title: Singing I will thus transform him;
scenes.place: Singing I will thus transform him;
scenes.reentry: I will hurl such hero-cowards, This one hither, that one thither,

scenes.title: Stamp him in the mire and bedding,
scenes.place: Stamp him in the mire and bedding,
scenes.reentry: In the rubbish of the stable.”

scenes.title: Angry then grew Wainamoinen,
scenes.place: Angry then grew Wainamoinen,
scenes.reentry: Wrathful waxed, and fiercely frowning, Self-composed he broke his silence,

scenes.title: And began his wondrous singing
scenes.place: And began his wondrous singing
scenes.reentry: Sang he not the tales of childhood, Children’s nonsense, wit of women,

scenes.title: Sang he rather bearded heroes,
scenes.place: Sang he rather bearded heroes,
scenes.reentry: That the children never heard of, That the boys and maidens knew not,

scenes.title: Known but half by bride and bridegroom,
scenes.place: Known but half by bride and bridegroom,
scenes.reentry: Known in part by many heroes, In these mournful days of evil,

scenes.title: Evil times our race befallen
scenes.place: Evil times our race befallen
scenes.reentry: Grandly sang wise Wainamoinen, Till the copper-bearing mountains,

scenes.title: And the flinty rocks and ledges
scenes.place: And the flinty rocks and ledges
scenes.reentry: Heard his magic tones and trembled; Mountain cliffs were torn to pieces,

scenes.title: All the ocean heaved and tumbled;
scenes.place: All the ocean heaved and tumbled;
scenes.reentry: And the distant hills re-echoed. Lo! the boastful Youkahainen

scenes.title: Is transfixed in silent wonder,
scenes.place: Is transfixed in silent wonder,
scenes.reentry: And his sledge with golden trimmings Floats like brushwood on the billows;

scenes.title: Sings his braces into reed-grass,
scenes.place: Sings his braces into reed-grass,
scenes.reentry: Sings his reins to twigs of willow, And to shrubs his golden cross-bench.

scenes.title: Lo! his birch-whip, pearl-enameled,
scenes.place: Lo! his birch-whip, pearl-enameled,
scenes.reentry: Floats a reed upon the border; Lo! his steed with golden forehead,

scenes.title: Stands a statue on the waters;
scenes.place: Stands a statue on the waters;
scenes.reentry: Hames and traces are as fir-boughs, And his collar, straw and sea-grass.

scenes.title: Still the minstrel sings enchantment,
scenes.place: Still the minstrel sings enchantment,
scenes.reentry: Sings his sword with golden handle, Sings it into gleam of lightning,

scenes.title: Hangs it in the sky above him;
scenes.place: Hangs it in the sky above him;
scenes.reentry: Sings his cross-bow, gaily painted, To a rainbow o’er the ocean;

scenes.title: Sings his quick and feathered arrows
scenes.place: Sings his quick and feathered arrows
scenes.reentry: Into hawks and screaming eagles; Sings his dog with bended muzzle,

scenes.title: Into block of stone beside him;
scenes.place: Into block of stone beside him;
scenes.reentry: Sings his cap from off his forehead, Sings it into wreaths of vapor;

scenes.title: From his hands he sings his gauntlets
scenes.place: From his hands he sings his gauntlets
scenes.reentry: Into rushes on the waters; Sings his vesture, purple-colored,

scenes.title: Into white clouds in the heavens;
scenes.place: Into white clouds in the heavens;
scenes.reentry: Sings his girdle, set with jewels, Into twinkling stars around him;

scenes.title: And alas! for Youkahainen,
scenes.place: And alas! for Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Sings him into deeps of quick-sand; Ever deeper, deeper, deeper,

scenes.title: In his torture, sinks the wizard,
scenes.place: In his torture, sinks the wizard,
scenes.reentry: To his belt in mud and water. Now it was that Youkahainen

scenes.title: Comprehended but too clearly
scenes.place: Comprehended but too clearly
scenes.reentry: What his folly, what the end was, Of the journey he had ventured,

scenes.title: Vainly he had undertaken
scenes.place: Vainly he had undertaken
scenes.reentry: For the glory of a contest With the grand, old Wainamoinen.

scenes.title: When at last young Youkahainen,
scenes.place: When at last young Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Pohyola’s old and sorry stripling, Strives his best to move his right foot,

scenes.title: But alas! the foot obeys not;
scenes.place: But alas! the foot obeys not;
scenes.reentry: When he strives to move his left foot, Lo! he finds it turned to flint-stone.

scenes.title: Thereupon sad Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Thereupon sad Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: In the deeps of desperation, And in earnest supplication,

scenes.title: Thus addresses Wainamoinen:
scenes.place: Thus addresses Wainamoinen:
scenes.reentry: “O thou wise and worthy minstrel, Thou the only true magician,

scenes.title: Cease I pray thee thine enchantment,
scenes.place: Cease I pray thee thine enchantment,
scenes.reentry: Only turn away thy magic, Let me leave this slough of horror,

scenes.title: Loose me from this stony prison,
scenes.place: Loose me from this stony prison,
scenes.reentry: Free me from this killing torment, I will pay a golden ransom.”

scenes.title: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen:
scenes.place: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen:
scenes.reentry: “What the ransom thou wilt give me If I cease from mine enchantment,

scenes.title: If I turn away my magic,
scenes.place: If I turn away my magic,
scenes.reentry: Lift thee from thy slough of horror, Loose thee from thy stony prison,

scenes.title: Free thee from thy killing torment?”
scenes.place: Free thee from thy killing torment?”
scenes.reentry: Answered youthful Youkahainen: “Have at home two magic cross-bows,

scenes.title: Pair of bows of wondrous power,
scenes.place: Pair of bows of wondrous power,
scenes.reentry: One so light a child can bend it, Only strength can bend the other,

scenes.title: Take of these the one that pleases.”
scenes.place: Take of these the one that pleases.”
scenes.reentry: Then the ancient Wainamoinen: “Do not wish thy magic cross-bows,

scenes.title: Have a few of such already,
scenes.place: Have a few of such already,
scenes.reentry: Thine to me are worse than useless; I have bows in great abundance,

scenes.title: Bows on every nail and rafter,
scenes.place: Bows on every nail and rafter,
scenes.reentry: Bows that laugh at all the hunters, Bows that go themselves a-hunting.”

scenes.title: Then the ancient Wainamoinen
scenes.place: Then the ancient Wainamoinen
scenes.reentry: Sang alas! poor Youkahainen Deeper into mud and water,

scenes.title: Deeper in the slough of torment
scenes.place: Deeper in the slough of torment
scenes.reentry: Youkahainen thus made answer: “Have at home two magic shallops,

scenes.title: Beautiful the boats and wondrous;
scenes.place: Beautiful the boats and wondrous;
scenes.reentry: One rides light upon the ocean, One is made for heavy burdens;

scenes.title: Take of these the one that pleases.”
scenes.place: Take of these the one that pleases.”
scenes.reentry: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen: “Do not wish thy magic shallops,

scenes.title: Have enough of such already;
scenes.place: Have enough of such already;
scenes.reentry: All my bays are full of shallops, All my shores are lined with shallops,

scenes.title: Some before the winds are sailors,
scenes.place: Some before the winds are sailors,
scenes.reentry: Some were built to sail against them.”

scenes.title: Still the minstrel of Wainola
scenes.place: Still the minstrel of Wainola
scenes.reentry: Sings again poor Youkahainen Deeper, deeper into torment,

scenes.title: Into quicksand to his girdle,
scenes.place: Into quicksand to his girdle,
scenes.reentry: Till the Lapland bard in anguish Speaks again to Wainamoinen: “Have at home two magic stallions,

scenes.title: One a racer, fleet as lightning,
scenes.place: One a racer, fleet as lightning,
scenes.reentry: One was born for heavy burdens; Take of these the one that pleases.”

scenes.title: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen:
scenes.place: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen:
scenes.reentry: “Neither do I wish thy stallions, Do not need thy hawk-limbed stallions,

scenes.title: Have enough of these already;
scenes.place: Have enough of these already;
scenes.reentry: Magic stallions swarm my stables, Eating corn at every manger,

scenes.title: Broad of back to hold the water,
scenes.place: Broad of back to hold the water,
scenes.reentry: Water on each croup in lakelets.”

scenes.title: Still the bard of Kalevala
scenes.place: Still the bard of Kalevala
scenes.reentry: Sings the hapless Lapland minstrel Deeper, deeper into torment,

scenes.title: To his shoulders into water
scenes.place: To his shoulders into water
scenes.reentry: Spake again young Youkahainen: “O thou ancient Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Thou the only true magician,
scenes.place: Thou the only true magician,
scenes.reentry: Cease I pray thee thine enchantment, Only turn away thy magic,

scenes.title: I will give thee gold abundant,
scenes.place: I will give thee gold abundant,
scenes.reentry: Countless stores of shining silver; From the wars my father brought it,

scenes.title: Brought it from the hard-fought battles.”
scenes.place: Brought it from the hard-fought battles.”
scenes.reentry: Spake the wise, old Wainamoinen: “For thy gold I have no longing,

scenes.title: Neither do I wish thy silver,
scenes.place: Neither do I wish thy silver,
scenes.reentry: Have enough of each already; Gold abundant fills my chambers,

scenes.title: On each nail hang bags of silver,
scenes.place: On each nail hang bags of silver,
scenes.reentry: Gold that glitters in the sunshine, Silver shining in the moonlight.”

scenes.title: Sank the braggart, Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Sank the braggart, Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Deeper in his slough of torment, To his chin in mud and water,

scenes.title: Ever praying, thus beseeching:
scenes.place: Ever praying, thus beseeching:
scenes.reentry: “O thou ancient Wainamoinen, Greatest of the old magicians,

scenes.title: Lift me from this pit of horror,
scenes.place: Lift me from this pit of horror,
scenes.reentry: From this prison-house of torture; I will give thee all my corn-fields,

scenes.title: Give thee all my corn in garners,
scenes.place: Give thee all my corn in garners,
scenes.reentry: Thus my hapless life to ransom, Thus to gain eternal freedom.”

scenes.title: Wainamoinen thus made answer:
scenes.place: Wainamoinen thus made answer:
scenes.reentry: “Take thy corn to other markets, Give thy garners to the needy;

scenes.title: I have corn in great abundance,
scenes.place: I have corn in great abundance,
scenes.reentry: Fields have I in every quarter, Corn in all my fields is growing;

scenes.title: One’s own fields are always richer,
scenes.place: One’s own fields are always richer,
scenes.reentry: One’s own grain is much the sweeter.”

scenes.title: Lapland’s young and reckless minstrel,
scenes.place: Lapland’s young and reckless minstrel,
scenes.reentry: Sorrow-laden, thus enchanted, Deeper sinks in mud and water,

scenes.title: Fear-enchained and full of anguish,
scenes.place: Fear-enchained and full of anguish,
scenes.reentry: In the mire, his beard bedrabbled, Mouth once boastful filled with sea-weed,

scenes.title: In the grass his teeth entangled,
scenes.place: In the grass his teeth entangled,
scenes.reentry: Youkahainen thus beseeches: “O thou ancient Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Wisest of the wisdom-singers,
scenes.place: Wisest of the wisdom-singers,
scenes.reentry: Cease at last thine incantations, Only turn away thy magic,

scenes.title: And my former life restore me,
scenes.place: And my former life restore me,
scenes.reentry: Lift me from this stifling torment, Free mine eyes from sand and water,

scenes.title: I will give thee sister, Aino,
scenes.place: I will give thee sister, Aino,
scenes.reentry: Fairest daughter of my mother, Bride of thine to be forever,

scenes.title: Bride of thine to do thy pleasure,
scenes.place: Bride of thine to do thy pleasure,
scenes.reentry: Sweep the rooms within thy cottage, Keep thy dwelling-place in order,

scenes.title: Rinse for thee the golden platters,
scenes.place: Rinse for thee the golden platters,
scenes.reentry: Spread thy couch with finest linens, For thy bed, weave golden covers,

scenes.title: Bake for thee the honey-biscuit.”
scenes.place: Bake for thee the honey-biscuit.”
scenes.reentry: Wainamoinen, old and truthful,

scenes.title: Finds at last the wished-for ransom,
scenes.place: Finds at last the wished-for ransom,
scenes.reentry: Lapland’s young and fairest daughter, Sister dear of Youkahainen;

scenes.title: Happy he, that he has won him,
scenes.place: Happy he, that he has won him,
scenes.reentry: In his age a beauteous maiden, Bride of his to be forever,

scenes.title: Pride and joy of Kalevala
scenes.place: Pride and joy of Kalevala
scenes.reentry: Now the happy Wainamoinen, Sits upon the rock of gladness,

scenes.title: Joyful on the rock of music,
scenes.place: Joyful on the rock of music,
scenes.reentry: Sings a little, sings and ceases, Sings again, and sings a third time,

scenes.title: Thus to break the spell of magic,
scenes.place: Thus to break the spell of magic,
scenes.reentry: Thus to lessen the enchantment, Thus the potent charm to banish.

scenes.title: As the magic spell is broken,
scenes.place: As the magic spell is broken,
scenes.reentry: Youkahainen, sad, but wiser, Drags his feet from out the quicksand,

scenes.title: Lifts his beard from out the water,
scenes.place: Lifts his beard from out the water,
scenes.reentry: From the rocks leads forth his courser, Brings his sledge back from the rushes,

scenes.title: Calls his whip back from the ocean,
scenes.place: Calls his whip back from the ocean,
scenes.reentry: Sets his golden sledge in order, Throws himself upon the cross-bench,

scenes.title: Snaps his whip and hies him homeward,
scenes.place: Snaps his whip and hies him homeward,
scenes.reentry: Hastens homeward, heavy-hearted, Sad indeed to meet his mother,

scenes.title: Aino’s mother, gray and aged
scenes.place: Aino’s mother, gray and aged
scenes.reentry: Careless thus he hastens homeward, Nears his home with noise and bustle,

scenes.title: Reckless drives against the pent-house,
scenes.place: Reckless drives against the pent-house,
scenes.reentry: Breaks the shafts against the portals, Breaks his handsome sledge in pieces.

scenes.title: Then his mother, quickly guessing,
scenes.place: Then his mother, quickly guessing,
scenes.reentry: Would have chided him for rashness, But the father interrupted: “Wherefore dost thou break thy snow-sledge,

scenes.title: Wherefore dash thy thills in fragments,
scenes.place: Wherefore dash thy thills in fragments,
scenes.reentry: Wherefore comest home so strangely, Why this rude and wild behavior?”

scenes.title: Now alas! poor Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Now alas! poor Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Cap awry upon his forehead, Falls to weeping, broken-hearted,

scenes.title: Head depressed and mind dejected,
scenes.place: Head depressed and mind dejected,
scenes.reentry: Eyes and lips expressing sadness, Answers not his anxious father.

scenes.title: Then the mother quickly asked him,
scenes.place: Then the mother quickly asked him,
scenes.reentry: Sought to find his cause for sorrow: “Tell me, first-born, why thou weepest,

scenes.title: Why thou weepest, heavy-hearted,
scenes.place: Why thou weepest, heavy-hearted,
scenes.reentry: Why thy mind is so dejected, Why thine eyes express such sadness.”

scenes.title: Youkahainen then made answer:
scenes.place: Youkahainen then made answer:
scenes.reentry: “Golden mother, ever faithful, Cause there is to me sufficient,

scenes.title: Cause enough in what has happened,
scenes.place: Cause enough in what has happened,
scenes.reentry: Bitter cause for this my sorrow, Cause for bitter tears and murmurs:

scenes.title: All my days will pass unhappy,
scenes.place: All my days will pass unhappy,
scenes.reentry: Since, O mother of my being, I have promised beauteous Aino,

scenes.title: Aino, thy beloved daughter,
scenes.place: Aino, thy beloved daughter,
scenes.reentry: Aino, my devoted sister, To decrepit Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Bride to be to him forever,
scenes.place: Bride to be to him forever,
scenes.reentry: Roof above him, prop beneath him, Fair companion at his fire-side.”

scenes.title: Joyful then arose the mother,
scenes.place: Joyful then arose the mother,
scenes.reentry: Clapped her hands in glee together, Thus addressing Youkahainen: “Weep no more, my son beloved,

scenes.title: Thou hast naught to cause thy weeping,
scenes.place: Thou hast naught to cause thy weeping,
scenes.reentry: Hast no reason for thy sorrow, Often I this hope have cherished;

scenes.title: Many years have I been praying
scenes.place: Many years have I been praying
scenes.reentry: That this mighty bard and hero, Wise and valiant Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Spouse should be to beauteous Aino,
scenes.place: Spouse should be to beauteous Aino,
scenes.reentry: Son-in-law to me, her mother.”

scenes.title: But the fair and lovely maiden,
scenes.place: But the fair and lovely maiden,
scenes.reentry: Sister dear of Youkahainen, Straightway fell to bitter weeping,

scenes.title: On the threshold wept and lingered,
scenes.place: On the threshold wept and lingered,
scenes.reentry: Wept all day and all the night long, Wept a second, then a third day,

scenes.title: Wept because a bitter sorrow
scenes.place: Wept because a bitter sorrow
scenes.reentry: On her youthful heart had fallen. Then the gray-haired mother asked her: “Why this weeping, lovely Aino?

scenes.title: Thou hast found a noble suitor,
scenes.place: Thou hast found a noble suitor,
scenes.reentry: Thou wilt rule his spacious dwelling, At his window sit and rest thee,

scenes.title: Rinse betimes his golden platters,
scenes.place: Rinse betimes his golden platters,
scenes.reentry: Walk a queen within his dwelling.” Thus replied the tearful Aino: “Mother dear, and all-forgiving,

scenes.title: Cause enough for this my sorrow,
scenes.place: Cause enough for this my sorrow,
scenes.reentry: Cause enough for bitter weeping: I must loose my sunny tresses,

scenes.title: Tresses beautiful and golden,
scenes.place: Tresses beautiful and golden,
scenes.reentry: Cannot deck my hair with jewels, Cannot bind my head with ribbons,

scenes.title: All to be hereafter hidden
scenes.place: All to be hereafter hidden
scenes.reentry: Underneath the linen bonnet That the wife must wear forever;

scenes.title: Weep at morning, weep at evening,
scenes.place: Weep at morning, weep at evening,
scenes.reentry: Weep alas! for waning beauty, Childhood vanished, youth departed,

scenes.title: Silver sunshine, golden moonlight,
scenes.place: Silver sunshine, golden moonlight,
scenes.reentry: Hope and pleasure of my childhood, Taken from me now forever,

scenes.title: And so soon to be forgotten
scenes.place: And so soon to be forgotten
scenes.reentry: At the tool-bench of my brother, At the window of my sister,

scenes.title: In the cottage of my father.”
scenes.place: In the cottage of my father.”
scenes.reentry: Spake again the gray-haired mother

scenes.title: To her wailing daughter Aino:
scenes.place: To her wailing daughter Aino:
scenes.reentry: “Cease thy sorrow, foolish maiden, By thy tears thou art ungrateful,

scenes.title: Reason none for thy repining,
scenes.place: Reason none for thy repining,
scenes.reentry: Not the slightest cause for weeping; Everywhere the silver sunshine

scenes.title: Falls as bright on other households;
scenes.place: Falls as bright on other households;
scenes.reentry: Not alone the moonlight glimmers Through thy father’s open windows,

scenes.title: On the work-bench of thy brother;
scenes.place: On the work-bench of thy brother;
scenes.reentry: Flowers bloom in every meadow, Berries grow on every mountain;

scenes.title: Thou canst go thyself and find them,
scenes.place: Thou canst go thyself and find them,
scenes.reentry: All the day long go and find them; Not alone thy brother’s meadows

scenes.title: Grow the beauteous vines and flowers;
scenes.place: Grow the beauteous vines and flowers;
scenes.reentry: Not alone thy father’s mountains Yield the ripe, nutritious berries;

scenes.title: Flowers bloom in other meadows,
scenes.place: Flowers bloom in other meadows,
scenes.reentry: Berries grow on other mountains, There as here, my lovely Aino.”

scenes.title: Rune Iv
scenes.place: Rune Iv
scenes.reentry: THE Fate OF Aino.

scenes.title: When the night had passed, the maiden,
scenes.place: When the night had passed, the maiden,
scenes.reentry: Sister fair of Youkahainen, Hastened early to the forest,

scenes.title: Birchen shoots for brooms to gather,
scenes.place: Birchen shoots for brooms to gather,
scenes.reentry: Went to gather birchen tassels; Bound a bundle for her father,

scenes.title: Bound a birch-broom for her mother,
scenes.place: Bound a birch-broom for her mother,
scenes.reentry: Silken tassels for her sister. Straightway then she hastened homeward,

scenes.title: By a foot-path left the forest;
scenes.place: By a foot-path left the forest;
scenes.reentry: As she neared the woodland border, Lo! the ancient Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Quickly spying out the maiden,
scenes.place: Quickly spying out the maiden,
scenes.reentry: As she left the birchen woodland, Trimly dressed in costly raiment,

scenes.title: And the minstrel thus addressed her:
scenes.place: And the minstrel thus addressed her:
scenes.reentry: “Aino, beauty of the Northland, Wear not, lovely maid, for others,

scenes.title: Only wear for me, sweet maiden,
scenes.place: Only wear for me, sweet maiden,
scenes.reentry: Golden cross upon thy bosom, Shining pearls upon thy shoulders;

scenes.title: Bind for me thine auburn tresses,
scenes.place: Bind for me thine auburn tresses,
scenes.reentry: Wear for me thy golden braidlets.” Thus the maiden quickly answered: “Not for thee and not for others,

scenes.title: Hang I from my neck the crosslet,
scenes.place: Hang I from my neck the crosslet,
scenes.reentry: Deck my hair with silken ribbons; Need no more the many trinkets

scenes.title: Brought to me by ship or shallop;
scenes.place: Brought to me by ship or shallop;
scenes.reentry: Sooner wear the simplest raiment, Feed upon the barley bread-crust,

scenes.title: Dwell forever with my mother
scenes.place: Dwell forever with my mother
scenes.reentry: In the cabin with my father.”

scenes.title: Then she threw the gold cross from her,
scenes.place: Then she threw the gold cross from her,
scenes.reentry: Tore the jewels from her fingers, Quickly loosed her shining necklace,

scenes.title: Quick untied her silken ribbons,
scenes.place: Quick untied her silken ribbons,
scenes.reentry: Cast them all away indignant Into forest ferns and flowers.

scenes.title: Thereupon the maiden, Aino,
scenes.place: Thereupon the maiden, Aino,
scenes.reentry: Hastened to her mother’s cottage.

scenes.title: At the window sat her father
scenes.place: At the window sat her father
scenes.reentry: Whittling on an oaken ax-helve: “Wherefore weepest, beauteous Aino,

scenes.title: Aino, my beloved daughter?”
scenes.place: Aino, my beloved daughter?”
scenes.reentry: “Cause enough for weeping, father,

scenes.title: Good the reasons for my mourning,
scenes.place: Good the reasons for my mourning,
scenes.reentry: This, the reason for my weeping, This, the cause of all my sorrow:

scenes.title: From my breast I tore the crosslet,
scenes.place: From my breast I tore the crosslet,
scenes.reentry: From my belt, the clasp of copper, From my waist, the belt of silver,

scenes.title: Golden was my pretty crosslet.”
scenes.place: Golden was my pretty crosslet.”
scenes.reentry: Near the door-way sat her brother,

scenes.title: Carving out a birchen ox-bow:
scenes.place: Carving out a birchen ox-bow:
scenes.reentry: “Why art weeping, lovely Aino, Aino, my devoted sister?”

scenes.title: Good the reasons for my mourning:
scenes.place: Good the reasons for my mourning:
scenes.reentry: Therefore come I as thou seest, Rings no longer on my fingers,

scenes.title: On my neck no pretty necklace;
scenes.place: On my neck no pretty necklace;
scenes.reentry: Golden were the rings thou gavest, And the necklace, pearls and silver!”

scenes.title: On the threshold sat her sister,
scenes.place: On the threshold sat her sister,
scenes.reentry: Weaving her a golden girdle: “Why art weeping, beauteous Aino,

scenes.title: Aino, my beloved sister?”
scenes.place: Aino, my beloved sister?”
scenes.reentry: “Cause enough for weeping, sister,

scenes.title: Good the reasons for my sorrow:
scenes.place: Good the reasons for my sorrow:
scenes.reentry: Therefore come I as thou seest, On my head no scarlet fillet,

scenes.title: In my hair no braids of silver,
scenes.place: In my hair no braids of silver,
scenes.reentry: On mine arms no purple ribbons, Round my neck no shining necklace,

scenes.title: On my breast no golden crosslet,
scenes.place: On my breast no golden crosslet,
scenes.reentry: In mine ears no golden ear-rings.”

scenes.title: Near the door-way of the dairy,
scenes.place: Near the door-way of the dairy,
scenes.reentry: Skimming cream, sat Aino’s mother. “Why art weeping, lovely Aino,

scenes.title: Aino, my devoted daughter?”
scenes.place: Aino, my devoted daughter?”
scenes.reentry: Thus the sobbing maiden answered: “Loving mother, all-forgiving,

scenes.title: Cause enough for this my weeping,
scenes.place: Cause enough for this my weeping,
scenes.reentry: Good the reasons for my sorrow, Therefore do I weep, dear mother:

scenes.title: I have been within the forest,
scenes.place: I have been within the forest,
scenes.reentry: Brooms to bind and shoots to gather, There to pluck some birchen tassels;

scenes.title: Bound a bundle for my father,
scenes.place: Bound a bundle for my father,
scenes.reentry: Bound a second for my mother, Bound a third one for my brother,

scenes.title: For my sister silken tassels
scenes.place: For my sister silken tassels
scenes.reentry: Straightway then I hastened homeward, By a foot-path left the forest;

scenes.title: As I reached the woodland border
scenes.place: As I reached the woodland border
scenes.reentry: Spake Osmoinen from the cornfield, Spake the ancient Wainamoinen: ‘Wear not, beauteous maid, for others,

scenes.title: Only wear for me, sweet maiden,
scenes.place: Only wear for me, sweet maiden,
scenes.reentry: On thy breast a golden crosslet, Shining pearls upon thy shoulders,

scenes.title: Bind for me thine auburn tresses,
scenes.place: Bind for me thine auburn tresses,
scenes.reentry: Weave for me thy silver braidlets.’ Then I threw the gold-cross from me,

scenes.title: Tore the jewels from my fingers,
scenes.place: Tore the jewels from my fingers,
scenes.reentry: Quickly loosed my shining necklace, Quick untied my silken ribbons,

scenes.title: Cast them all away indignant,
scenes.place: Cast them all away indignant,
scenes.reentry: Into forest ferns and flowers. Then I thus addressed the singer: ‘Not for thee and not for others,

scenes.title: Hang I from my neck the crosslet,
scenes.place: Hang I from my neck the crosslet,
scenes.reentry: Deck my hair with silken ribbons; Need no more the many trinkets,

scenes.title: Brought to me by ship and shallop;
scenes.place: Brought to me by ship and shallop;
scenes.reentry: Sooner wear the simplest raiment, Feed upon the barley bread-crust,

scenes.title: Dwell forever with my mother
scenes.place: Dwell forever with my mother
scenes.reentry: In the cabin with my father.’”

scenes.title: Thus the gray-haired mother answered
scenes.place: Thus the gray-haired mother answered
scenes.reentry: Aino, her beloved daughter: “Weep no more, my lovely maiden,

scenes.title: Waste no more of thy sweet young-life;
scenes.place: Waste no more of thy sweet young-life;
scenes.reentry: One year eat thou my sweet butter, It will make thee strong and ruddy;

scenes.title: Eat another year fresh bacon,
scenes.place: Eat another year fresh bacon,
scenes.reentry: It will make thee tall and queenly; Eat a third year only dainties,

scenes.title: It will make thee fair and lovely
scenes.place: It will make thee fair and lovely
scenes.reentry: Now make haste to yonder hill-top, To the store-house on the mountain,

scenes.title: Open there the large compartment,
scenes.place: Open there the large compartment,
scenes.reentry: Thou will find it filled with boxes, Chests and cases, trunks and boxes;

scenes.title: Open thou the box, the largest,
scenes.place: Open thou the box, the largest,
scenes.reentry: Lift away the gaudy cover, Thou will find six golden girdles,

scenes.title: Seven rainbow-tinted dresses,
scenes.place: Seven rainbow-tinted dresses,
scenes.reentry: Woven by the Moon’s fair daughters, Fashioned by the Sun’s sweet virgins.

scenes.title: In my young years once I wandered,
scenes.place: In my young years once I wandered,
scenes.reentry: As a maiden on the mountains, In the happy days of childhood,

scenes.title: Hunting berries in the coppice;
scenes.place: Hunting berries in the coppice;
scenes.reentry: There by chance I heard the daughters Of the Moon as they were weaving;

scenes.title: There I also heard the daughters
scenes.place: There I also heard the daughters
scenes.reentry: Of the Sun as they were spinning On the red rims of the cloudlets,

scenes.title: O’er the blue edge of the forest,
scenes.place: O’er the blue edge of the forest,
scenes.reentry: On the border of the pine-wood, On a high and distant mountain.

scenes.title: I approached them, drawing nearer,
scenes.place: I approached them, drawing nearer,
scenes.reentry: Stole myself within their hearing, Then began I to entreat them,

scenes.title: Thus besought them, gently pleading:
scenes.place: Thus besought them, gently pleading:
scenes.reentry: ‘Give thy silver, Moon’s fair daughters, To a poor, but worthy maiden;

scenes.title: Give thy gold, O Sun’s sweet virgins,
scenes.place: Give thy gold, O Sun’s sweet virgins,
scenes.reentry: To this maiden, young and needy.’ Thereupon the Moon’s fair daughters

scenes.title: Gave me silver from their coffers;
scenes.place: Gave me silver from their coffers;
scenes.reentry: And the Sun’s sweet shining virgins Gave me gold from their abundance,

scenes.title: Gold to deck my throbbing temples,
scenes.place: Gold to deck my throbbing temples,
scenes.reentry: For my hair the shining silver. Then I hastened joyful homeward,

scenes.title: Richly laden with my treasures,
scenes.place: Richly laden with my treasures,
scenes.reentry: Happy to my mother’s cottage; Wore them one day, than a second,

scenes.title: Then a third day also wore them,
scenes.place: Then a third day also wore them,
scenes.reentry: Took the gold then from my temples, From my hair I took the silver,

scenes.title: Careful laid them in their boxes,
scenes.place: Careful laid them in their boxes,
scenes.reentry: Many seasons have they lain there, Have not seen them since my childhood.

scenes.title: Deck thy brow with silken ribbon,
scenes.place: Deck thy brow with silken ribbon,
scenes.reentry: Trim with gold thy throbbing temples, And thy neck with pearly necklace,

scenes.title: Hang the gold-cross on thy bosom,
scenes.place: Hang the gold-cross on thy bosom,
scenes.reentry: Robe thyself in pure, white linen Spun from flax of finest fiber;

scenes.title: Wear withal the richest short-frock,
scenes.place: Wear withal the richest short-frock,
scenes.reentry: Fasten it with golden girdle; On thy feet, put silken stockings,

scenes.title: With the shoes of finest leather;
scenes.place: With the shoes of finest leather;
scenes.reentry: Deck thy hair with golden braidlets, Bind it well with threads of silver;

scenes.title: Trim with rings thy fairy fingers,
scenes.place: Trim with rings thy fairy fingers,
scenes.reentry: And thy hands with dainty ruffles; Come bedecked then to thy chamber,

scenes.title: Thus return to this thy household,
scenes.place: Thus return to this thy household,
scenes.reentry: To the greeting of thy kindred, To the joy of all that know thee,

scenes.title: Flushed thy cheeks as ruddy berries,
scenes.place: Flushed thy cheeks as ruddy berries,
scenes.reentry: Coming as thy father’s sunbeam, Walking beautiful and queenly,

scenes.title: Far more beautiful than moonlight.”
scenes.place: Far more beautiful than moonlight.”
scenes.reentry: Thus she spake to weeping Aino,

scenes.title: Thus the mother to her daughter;
scenes.place: Thus the mother to her daughter;
scenes.reentry: But the maiden, little hearing, Does not heed her mother’s wishes;

scenes.title: Straightway hastens to the court-yard,
scenes.place: Straightway hastens to the court-yard,
scenes.reentry: There to weep in bitter sorrow, All alone to weep in anguish.

scenes.title: Waiting long the wailing Aino
scenes.place: Waiting long the wailing Aino
scenes.reentry: Thus at last soliloquizes: “Unto what can I now liken

scenes.title: Happy homes and joys of fortune?
scenes.place: Happy homes and joys of fortune?
scenes.reentry: Like the waters in the river, Like the waves in yonder lakelet,

scenes.title: Like the crystal waters flowing
scenes.place: Like the crystal waters flowing
scenes.reentry: Unto what, the biting sorrow Of the child of cold misfortune?

scenes.title: Like the spirit of the sea-duck,
scenes.place: Like the spirit of the sea-duck,
scenes.reentry: Like the icicle in winter, Water in the well imprisoned.

scenes.title: Often roamed my mind in childhood,
scenes.place: Often roamed my mind in childhood,
scenes.reentry: When a maiden free and merry, Happily through fen and fallow,

scenes.title: Gamboled on the meads with lambkins,
scenes.place: Gamboled on the meads with lambkins,
scenes.reentry: Lingered with the ferns and flowers, Knowing neither pain nor trouble;

scenes.title: Now my mind is filled with sorrow,
scenes.place: Now my mind is filled with sorrow,
scenes.reentry: Wanders though the bog and stubble, Wanders weary through the brambles,

scenes.title: Roams throughout the dismal forest,
scenes.place: Roams throughout the dismal forest,
scenes.reentry: Till my life is filled with darkness, And my spirit white with anguish.

scenes.title: Better had it been for Aino
scenes.place: Better had it been for Aino
scenes.reentry: Had she never seen the sunlight, Or if born had died an infant,

scenes.title: Had not lived to be a maiden
scenes.place: Had not lived to be a maiden
scenes.reentry: In these days of sin and sorrow, Underneath a star so luckless.

scenes.title: Better had it been for Aino,
scenes.place: Better had it been for Aino,
scenes.reentry: Had she died upon the eighth day After seven nights had vanished;

scenes.title: Needed then but little linen,
scenes.place: Needed then but little linen,
scenes.reentry: Needed but a little coffin, And a grave of smallest measure;

scenes.title: Mother would have mourned a little,
scenes.place: Mother would have mourned a little,
scenes.reentry: Father too perhaps a trifle, Sister would have wept the day through,

scenes.title: Brother might have shed a tear-drop,
scenes.place: Brother might have shed a tear-drop,
scenes.reentry: Thus had ended all the mourning.”

scenes.title: Thus poor Aino wept and murmured,
scenes.place: Thus poor Aino wept and murmured,
scenes.reentry: Wept one day, and then a second, Wept a third from morn till even,

scenes.title: When again her mother asked her:
scenes.place: When again her mother asked her:
scenes.reentry: “Why this weeping, fairest daughter, Darling daughter, why this grieving?”

scenes.title: Thus the tearful maiden answered:
scenes.place: Thus the tearful maiden answered:
scenes.reentry: “Therefore do I weep and sorrow, Wretched maiden all my life long,

scenes.title: Since poor Aino, thou hast given,
scenes.place: Since poor Aino, thou hast given,
scenes.reentry: Since thy daughter thou hast promised To the aged Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Comfort to his years declining,
scenes.place: Comfort to his years declining,
scenes.reentry: Prop to stay him when he totters, In the storm a roof above him,

scenes.title: In his home a cloak around him;
scenes.place: In his home a cloak around him;
scenes.reentry: Better far if thou hadst sent me Far below the salt-sea surges,

scenes.title: To become the whiting’s sister,
scenes.place: To become the whiting’s sister,
scenes.reentry: And the friend of perch and salmon; Better far to ride the billows,

scenes.title: Swim the sea-foam as a mermaid,
scenes.place: Swim the sea-foam as a mermaid,
scenes.reentry: And the friend of nimble fishes, Than to be an old man’s solace,

scenes.title: Prop to stay him when he totters,
scenes.place: Prop to stay him when he totters,
scenes.reentry: Hand to aid him when he trembles, Arm to guide him when he falters,

scenes.title: Strength to give him when he weakens;
scenes.place: Strength to give him when he weakens;
scenes.reentry: Better be the whiting’s sister And the friend of perch and salmon,

scenes.title: Than an old man’s slave and darling.”
scenes.place: Than an old man’s slave and darling.”
scenes.reentry: Ending thus she left her mother,

scenes.title: Straightway hastened to the mountain,
scenes.place: Straightway hastened to the mountain,
scenes.reentry: To the store-house on the summit, Opened there the box the largest,

scenes.title: From the box six lids she lifted,
scenes.place: From the box six lids she lifted,
scenes.reentry: Found therein six golden girdles, Silken dresses seven in number.

scenes.title: Choosing such as pleased her fancy,
scenes.place: Choosing such as pleased her fancy,
scenes.reentry: She adorned herself as bidden, Robed herself to look her fairest,

scenes.title: Gold upon her throbbing temples,
scenes.place: Gold upon her throbbing temples,
scenes.reentry: In her hair the shining silver, On her shoulders purple ribbons,

scenes.title: Band of blue around her forehead,
scenes.place: Band of blue around her forehead,
scenes.reentry: Golden cross, and rings, and jewels, Fitting ornaments to beauty.

scenes.title: Now she leaves her many treasures,
scenes.place: Now she leaves her many treasures,
scenes.reentry: Leaves the store-house on the mountain, Filled with gold and silver trinkets,

scenes.title: Wanders over field and meadow,
scenes.place: Wanders over field and meadow,
scenes.reentry: Over stone-fields waste and barren, Wanders on through fen and forest,

scenes.title: Through the forest vast and cheerless,
scenes.place: Through the forest vast and cheerless,
scenes.reentry: Wanders hither, wanders thither, Singing careless as she wanders,

scenes.title: This her mournful song and echo:
scenes.place: This her mournful song and echo:
scenes.reentry: “Woe is me, my life hard-fated! Woe to Aino, broken-hearted!

scenes.title: Torture racks my heart and temples,
scenes.place: Torture racks my heart and temples,
scenes.reentry: Yet the sting would not be deeper, Nor the pain and anguish greater,

scenes.title: If beneath this weight of sorrow,
scenes.place: If beneath this weight of sorrow,
scenes.reentry: In my saddened heart’s dejection, I should yield my life forever,

scenes.title: Now unhappy, I should perish!
scenes.place: Now unhappy, I should perish!
scenes.reentry: Lo! the time has come for Aino From this cruel world to hasten,

scenes.title: To the kingdom of Tuoni,
scenes.place: To the kingdom of Tuoni,
scenes.reentry: To the realm of the departed, To the isle of the hereafter.

scenes.title: Weep no more for me, O Father,
scenes.place: Weep no more for me, O Father,
scenes.reentry: Mother dear, withhold thy censure, Lovely sister, dry thine eyelids,

scenes.title: Do not mourn me, dearest brother,
scenes.place: Do not mourn me, dearest brother,
scenes.reentry: When I sink beneath the sea-foam, Make my home in salmon-grottoes,

scenes.title: Make my bed in crystal waters,
scenes.place: Make my bed in crystal waters,
scenes.reentry: Water-ferns my couch and pillow.”

scenes.title: All day long poor Aino wandered,
scenes.place: All day long poor Aino wandered,
scenes.reentry: All the next day, sad and weary, So the third from morn till evening,

scenes.title: Till the cruel night enwrapped her,
scenes.place: Till the cruel night enwrapped her,
scenes.reentry: As she reached the sandy margin, Reached the cold and dismal sea-shore,

scenes.title: Sat upon the rock of sorrow,
scenes.place: Sat upon the rock of sorrow,
scenes.reentry: Sat alone in cold and darkness, Listened only to the music

scenes.title: Of the winds and rolling billows,
scenes.place: Of the winds and rolling billows,
scenes.reentry: Singing all the dirge of Aino. All that night the weary maiden

scenes.title: Wept and wandered on the border
scenes.place: Wept and wandered on the border
scenes.reentry: Through the sand and sea-washed pebbles.

scenes.title: As the day dawns, looking round her,
scenes.place: As the day dawns, looking round her,
scenes.reentry: She beholds three water-maidens, On a headland jutting seaward,

scenes.title: Water-maidens four in number,
scenes.place: Water-maidens four in number,
scenes.reentry: Sitting on the wave-lashed ledges, Swimming now upon the billows,

scenes.title: Now upon the rocks reposing
scenes.place: Now upon the rocks reposing
scenes.reentry: Quick the weeping maiden, Aino, Hastens there to join the mermaids,

scenes.title: Fairy maidens of the waters
scenes.place: Fairy maidens of the waters
scenes.reentry: Weeping Aino, now disrobing, Lays aside with care her garments,

scenes.title: Hangs her silk robes on the alders,
scenes.place: Hangs her silk robes on the alders,
scenes.reentry: Drops her gold-cross on the sea-shore, On the aspen hangs her ribbons,

scenes.title: On the rocks her silken stockings,
scenes.place: On the rocks her silken stockings,
scenes.reentry: On the grass her shoes of deer-skin, In the sand her shining necklace,

scenes.title: With her rings and other jewels
scenes.place: With her rings and other jewels
scenes.reentry: Out at sea a goodly distance,

scenes.title: Stood a rock of rainbow colors,
scenes.place: Stood a rock of rainbow colors,
scenes.reentry: Glittering in silver sunlight. Toward it springs the hapless maiden,

scenes.title: Thither swims the lovely Aino,
scenes.place: Thither swims the lovely Aino,
scenes.reentry: Up the standing-stone has clambered, Wishing there to rest a moment,

scenes.title: Rest upon the rock of beauty;
scenes.place: Rest upon the rock of beauty;
scenes.reentry: When upon a sudden swaying To and fro among the billows,

scenes.title: With a crash and roar of waters
scenes.place: With a crash and roar of waters
scenes.reentry: Falls the stone of many colors, Falls upon the very bottom

scenes.title: Of the deep and boundless blue-sea
scenes.place: Of the deep and boundless blue-sea
scenes.reentry: With the stone of rainbow colors, Falls the weeping maiden, Aino,

scenes.title: Clinging to its craggy edges,
scenes.place: Clinging to its craggy edges,
scenes.reentry: Sinking far below the surface, To the bottom of the blue-sea.

scenes.title: Thus the weeping maiden vanished,
scenes.place: Thus the weeping maiden vanished,
scenes.reentry: Thus poor Aino sank and perished, Singing as the stone descended,

scenes.title: Chanting thus as she departed:
scenes.place: Chanting thus as she departed:
scenes.reentry: “Once to swim I sought the sea-side, There to sport among the billows;

scenes.title: With the stone of many colors
scenes.place: With the stone of many colors
scenes.reentry: Sank poor Aino to the bottom Of the deep and boundless blue-sea,

scenes.title: Like a pretty son-bird perished
scenes.place: Like a pretty son-bird perished
scenes.reentry: Never come a-fishing, father, To the borders of these waters,

scenes.title: Never during all thy life-time,
scenes.place: Never during all thy life-time,
scenes.reentry: As thou lovest daughter Aino.

scenes.title: There to sport among the billows;
scenes.place: There to sport among the billows;
scenes.reentry: With the stone of many colors, Sank poor Aino to the bottom

scenes.title: Of the deep and boundless blue-sea,
scenes.place: Of the deep and boundless blue-sea,
scenes.reentry: Like a pretty song-bird perished. Never mix thy bread, dear mother,

scenes.title: With the blue-sea’s foam and waters,
scenes.place: With the blue-sea’s foam and waters,
scenes.reentry: Never during all thy life-time, As thou lovest daughter Aino.

scenes.title: There to sport among the billows;
scenes.place: There to sport among the billows;
scenes.reentry: With the stone of many colors Sank poor Aino to the bottom

scenes.title: Of the deep and boundless blue-sea,
scenes.place: Of the deep and boundless blue-sea,
scenes.reentry: Like a pretty song-bird perished. Never bring thy prancing war-horse,

scenes.title: Never bring thy royal racer,
scenes.place: Never bring thy royal racer,
scenes.reentry: Never bring thy steeds to water, To the borders of the blue-sea,

scenes.title: Never during all thy life-time,
scenes.place: Never during all thy life-time,
scenes.reentry: As thou lovest sister Aino.

scenes.title: There to sport among the billows;
scenes.place: There to sport among the billows;
scenes.reentry: With the stone of many colors Sank poor Aino to the bottom

scenes.title: Of the deep and boundless blue-sea,
scenes.place: Of the deep and boundless blue-sea,
scenes.reentry: Like a pretty song-bird perished. Never come to lave thine eyelids

scenes.title: In this rolling wave and sea-foam,
scenes.place: In this rolling wave and sea-foam,
scenes.reentry: Never during all thy life-time, As thou lovest sister Aino.

scenes.title: All the waters in the blue-sea
scenes.place: All the waters in the blue-sea
scenes.reentry: Shall be blood of Aino’s body; All the fish that swim these waters

scenes.title: Shall be Aino’s flesh forever;
scenes.place: Shall be Aino’s flesh forever;
scenes.reentry: All the willows on the sea-side Shall be Aino’s ribs hereafter;

scenes.title: All the sea-grass on the margin
scenes.place: All the sea-grass on the margin
scenes.reentry: Will have grown from Aino’s tresses.”

scenes.title: Thus at last the maiden vanished,
scenes.place: Thus at last the maiden vanished,
scenes.reentry: Thus the lovely Aino perished. Who will tell the cruel story,

scenes.title: Who will bear the evil tidings
scenes.place: Who will bear the evil tidings
scenes.reentry: To the cottage of her mother, Once the home of lovely Aino?

scenes.title: Will the bear repeat the story,
scenes.place: Will the bear repeat the story,
scenes.reentry: Tell the tidings to her mother? Nay, the bear must not be herald,

scenes.title: He would slay the herds of cattle
scenes.place: He would slay the herds of cattle
scenes.reentry: Who then tell the cruel story, Who will bear the evil tidings

scenes.title: To the cottage of her father,
scenes.place: To the cottage of her father,
scenes.reentry: Once the home of lovely Aino? Shall the wolf repeat the story,

scenes.title: Tell the sad news to her father?
scenes.place: Tell the sad news to her father?
scenes.reentry: Nay, the wolf must not be herald, He would eat the gentle lambkins.

scenes.title: Who then tell the cruel story,
scenes.place: Who then tell the cruel story,
scenes.reentry: Who will bear the evil tidings. To the cottage of her sister?

scenes.title: Will the fox repeat the story
scenes.place: Will the fox repeat the story
scenes.reentry: Tell the tidings to her sister? Nay, the fox must not be herald,

scenes.title: He would eat the ducks and chickens
scenes.place: He would eat the ducks and chickens
scenes.reentry: Who then tell the cruel story,

scenes.title: Who will bear the evil tidings
scenes.place: Who will bear the evil tidings
scenes.reentry: To the cottage of her brother, Once the home of lovely Aino?

scenes.title: Shall the hare repeat the story,
scenes.place: Shall the hare repeat the story,
scenes.reentry: Bear the sad news to her brother? Yea, the hare shall be the herald,

scenes.title: Tell to all the cruel story
scenes.place: Tell to all the cruel story
scenes.reentry: Thus the harmless hare makes answer: “I will bear the evil tidings

scenes.title: To the former home of Aino,
scenes.place: To the former home of Aino,
scenes.reentry: Tell the story to her kindred.”

scenes.title: Swiftly flew the long-eared herald,
scenes.place: Swiftly flew the long-eared herald,
scenes.reentry: Like the winds he hastened onward, Galloped swift as flight of eagles;

scenes.title: Neck awry he bounded forward
scenes.place: Neck awry he bounded forward
scenes.reentry: Till he gained the wished-for cottage, Once the home of lovely Aino.

scenes.title: Silent was the home, and vacant;
scenes.place: Silent was the home, and vacant;
scenes.reentry: So he hastened to the bath-house, Found therein a group of maidens,

scenes.title: Working each upon a birch-broom
scenes.place: Working each upon a birch-broom
scenes.reentry: Sat the hare upon the threshold, And the maidens thus addressed him: “Hie there, Long-legs, or we’ll roast thee,

scenes.title: Hie there, Big-eye, or we’ll stew thee,
scenes.place: Hie there, Big-eye, or we’ll stew thee,
scenes.reentry: Roast thee for our lady’s breakfast, Stew thee for our master’s dinner,

scenes.title: Make of thee a meal for Aino,
scenes.place: Make of thee a meal for Aino,
scenes.reentry: And her brother, Youkahainen! Better therefore thou shouldst gallop

scenes.title: To thy burrow in the mountains,
scenes.place: To thy burrow in the mountains,
scenes.reentry: Than be roasted for our dinners.”

scenes.title: Then the haughty hare made answer,
scenes.place: Then the haughty hare made answer,
scenes.reentry: Chanting thus the fate of Aino: “Think ye not I journey hither,

scenes.title: To be roasted in the skillet,
scenes.place: To be roasted in the skillet,
scenes.reentry: To be stewed in yonder kettle; Let fell Lempo fill thy tables!

scenes.title: I have come with evil tidings,
scenes.place: I have come with evil tidings,
scenes.reentry: Come to tell the cruel story Of the flight and death of Aino,

scenes.title: Sister dear of Youkahainen
scenes.place: Sister dear of Youkahainen
scenes.reentry: With the stone of many colors Sank poor Aino to the bottom

scenes.title: Of the deep and boundless waters,
scenes.place: Of the deep and boundless waters,
scenes.reentry: Like a pretty song-bird perished; Hung her ribbons on the aspen,

scenes.title: Left her gold-cross on the sea-shore,
scenes.place: Left her gold-cross on the sea-shore,
scenes.reentry: Silken robes upon the alders, On the rocks her silken stockings,

scenes.title: On the grass her shoes of deer-skin,
scenes.place: On the grass her shoes of deer-skin,
scenes.reentry: In the sand her shining necklace, In the sand her rings and jewels;

scenes.title: In the waves, the lovely Aino,
scenes.place: In the waves, the lovely Aino,
scenes.reentry: Sleeping on the very bottom Of the deep and boundless blue-sea,

scenes.title: In the caverns of the salmon,
scenes.place: In the caverns of the salmon,
scenes.reentry: There to be the whiting’s sister And the friend of nimble fishes.”

scenes.title: Sadly weeps the ancient mother
scenes.place: Sadly weeps the ancient mother
scenes.reentry: From her blue-eyes bitter tear-drops, As in sad and wailing measures,

scenes.title: Broken-hearted thus she answers:
scenes.place: Broken-hearted thus she answers:
scenes.reentry: “Listen, all ye mothers, listen, Learn from me a tale of wisdom:

scenes.title: Never urge unwilling daughters
scenes.place: Never urge unwilling daughters
scenes.reentry: From the dwellings of their fathers, To the bridegrooms that they love not,

scenes.title: Not as I, inhuman mother,
scenes.place: Not as I, inhuman mother,
scenes.reentry: Drove away my lovely Aino, Fairest daughter of the Northland.”

scenes.title: Sadly weeps the gray-haired mother,
scenes.place: Sadly weeps the gray-haired mother,
scenes.reentry: And the tears that fall are bitter, Flowing down her wrinkled visage,

scenes.title: Till they trickle on her bosom;
scenes.place: Till they trickle on her bosom;
scenes.reentry: Then across her heaving bosom, Till they reach her garment’s border;

scenes.title: Then adown her silken stockings,
scenes.place: Then adown her silken stockings,
scenes.reentry: Till they touch her shoes of deer-skin; Then beneath her shoes of deer-skin,

scenes.title: Flowing on and flowing ever,
scenes.place: Flowing on and flowing ever,
scenes.reentry: Part to earth as its possession, Part to water as its portion.

scenes.title: As the tear-drops fall and mingle,
scenes.place: As the tear-drops fall and mingle,
scenes.reentry: Form they streamlets three in number, And their source, the mother’s eyelids,

scenes.title: Streamlets formed from pearly tear-drops,
scenes.place: Streamlets formed from pearly tear-drops,
scenes.reentry: Flowing on like little rivers, And each streamlet larger growing,

scenes.title: Soon becomes a rushing torrent;
scenes.place: Soon becomes a rushing torrent;
scenes.reentry: In each rushing, roaring torrent, There a cataract is foaming,

scenes.title: Foaming in the silver sunlight;
scenes.place: Foaming in the silver sunlight;
scenes.reentry: From the cataract’s commotion Rise three pillared rocks in grandeur;

scenes.title: From each rock, upon the summit,
scenes.place: From each rock, upon the summit,
scenes.reentry: Grow three hillocks clothed in verdure; From each hillock, speckled birches,

scenes.title: Three in number, struggle skyward;
scenes.place: Three in number, struggle skyward;
scenes.reentry: On the summit of each birch-tree Sits a golden cuckoo calling,

scenes.title: And the three sing, all in concord:
scenes.place: And the three sing, all in concord:
scenes.reentry: “Love! O Love!” the first one calleth; Sings the second, “Suitor! Suitor!”

scenes.title: And the third one calls and echoes,
scenes.place: And the third one calls and echoes,
scenes.reentry: “Consolation! Consolation!” He that “Love! O Love!” is calling,

scenes.title: Calls three moons and calls unceasing,
scenes.place: Calls three moons and calls unceasing,
scenes.reentry: For the love-rejecting maiden Sleeping in the deep sea-castles.

scenes.title: He that “Suitor! Suitor!” singeth,
scenes.place: He that “Suitor! Suitor!” singeth,
