scenes.reentry: Sings six moons and sings unceasing For the suitor that forever

scenes.title: Sings and sues without a hearing
scenes.place: Sings and sues without a hearing
scenes.reentry: He that sadly sings and echoes, “Consolation! Consolation!”

scenes.title: Sings unceasing all his life long
scenes.place: Sings unceasing all his life long
scenes.reentry: For the broken-hearted mother That must mourn and weep forever.

scenes.title: When the lone and wretched mother
scenes.place: When the lone and wretched mother
scenes.reentry: Heard the sacred cuckoo singing, Spake she thus, and sorely weeping: “When I hear the cuckoo calling,

scenes.title: Then my heart is filled with sorrow;
scenes.place: Then my heart is filled with sorrow;
scenes.reentry: Tears unlock my heavy eyelids, Flow adown my furrowed visage,

scenes.title: Tears as large as silver sea pearls;
scenes.place: Tears as large as silver sea pearls;
scenes.reentry: Older grow my wearied elbows, Weaker ply my aged fingers,

scenes.title: Wearily, in all its members,
scenes.place: Wearily, in all its members,
scenes.reentry: Does my body shake in palsy, When I hear the cuckoo singing,

scenes.title: Rune V
scenes.place: Rune V
scenes.reentry: Wainavoinen’S Lamentation.

scenes.title: Far and wide the tidings travelled,
scenes.place: Far and wide the tidings travelled,
scenes.reentry: Far away men heard the story Of the flight and death of Aino,

scenes.title: Sister dear of Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Sister dear of Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Fairest daughter of creation.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, brave and truthful,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, brave and truthful,
scenes.reentry: Straightway fell to bitter weeping, Wept at morning, wept at evening,

scenes.title: Sleepless, wept the dreary night long,
scenes.place: Sleepless, wept the dreary night long,
scenes.reentry: That his Aino had departed, That the maiden thus had vanished,

scenes.title: Thus had sunk upon the bottom
scenes.place: Thus had sunk upon the bottom
scenes.reentry: Of the blue-sea, deep and boundless.

scenes.title: Filled with grief, the ancient singer,
scenes.place: Filled with grief, the ancient singer,
scenes.reentry: Wainamoinen of the Northland, Heavy-hearted, sorely weeping,

scenes.title: Hastened to the restless waters,
scenes.place: Hastened to the restless waters,
scenes.reentry: This the suitor’s prayer and question: “Tell, Untamo, tell me, dreamer,

scenes.title: Tell me, Indolence, thy visions,
scenes.place: Tell me, Indolence, thy visions,
scenes.reentry: Where the water-gods may linger, Where may rest Wellamo’s maidens?”

scenes.title: Then Untamo thus made answer,
scenes.place: Then Untamo thus made answer,
scenes.reentry: Lazily he told his dreamings: “Over there, the mermaid-dwellings,

scenes.title: Yonder live Wellamo’s maidens,
scenes.place: Yonder live Wellamo’s maidens,
scenes.reentry: On the headland robed in verdure, On the forest-covered island,

scenes.title: In the deep, pellucid waters,
scenes.place: In the deep, pellucid waters,
scenes.reentry: On the purple-colored sea-shore; Yonder is the home of sea-maids,

scenes.title: There the maidens of Wellamo,
scenes.place: There the maidens of Wellamo,
scenes.reentry: Live there in their sea-side chambers, Rest within their water-caverns,

scenes.title: On the rocks of rainbow colors,
scenes.place: On the rocks of rainbow colors,
scenes.reentry: On the juttings of the sea-cliffs.”

scenes.title: Straightway hastens Wainamoinen
scenes.place: Straightway hastens Wainamoinen
scenes.reentry: To a boat-house on the sea-shore, Looks with care upon the fish-hooks,

scenes.title: And the lines he well considers;
scenes.place: And the lines he well considers;
scenes.reentry: Lines, and hooks, and poles, and fish-nets, Places in a boat of copper,

scenes.title: Then begins he swiftly rowing
scenes.place: Then begins he swiftly rowing
scenes.reentry: To the forest-covered island, To the point enrobed in verdure,

scenes.title: To the purple-colored headland,
scenes.place: To the purple-colored headland,
scenes.reentry: Where the sea-nymphs live and linger. Hardly does he reach the island

scenes.title: Ere the minstrel starts to angle;
scenes.place: Ere the minstrel starts to angle;
scenes.reentry: Far away he throws his fish-hook, Trolls it quickly through the waters,

scenes.title: Turning on a copper swivel
scenes.place: Turning on a copper swivel
scenes.reentry: Dangling from a silver fish-line, Golden is the hook he uses.

scenes.title: Now he tries his silken fish-net,
scenes.place: Now he tries his silken fish-net,
scenes.reentry: Angles long, and angles longer, Angles one day, then a second,

scenes.title: In the morning, in the evening,
scenes.place: In the morning, in the evening,
scenes.reentry: Angles at the hour of noontide, Many days and nights he angles,

scenes.title: Till at last, one sunny morning,
scenes.place: Till at last, one sunny morning,
scenes.reentry: Strikes a fish of magic powers, Plays like salmon on his fish-line,

scenes.title: Lashing waves across the waters,
scenes.place: Lashing waves across the waters,
scenes.reentry: Till at length the fish exhausted Falls a victim to the angler,

scenes.title: Safely landed in the bottom
scenes.place: Safely landed in the bottom
scenes.reentry: Of the hero’s boat of copper.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, proudly viewing,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, proudly viewing,
scenes.reentry: Speaks these words in wonder guessing: “This the fairest of all sea-fish,

scenes.title: Never have I seen its equal,
scenes.place: Never have I seen its equal,
scenes.reentry: Smoother surely than the salmon, Brighter-spotted than the trout is,

scenes.title: Grayer than the pike of Suomi,
scenes.place: Grayer than the pike of Suomi,
scenes.reentry: Has less fins than any female, Not the fins of any male fish,

scenes.title: Not the stripes of sea-born maidens,
scenes.place: Not the stripes of sea-born maidens,
scenes.reentry: Not the belt of any mermaid, Not the ears of any song-bird,

scenes.title: Somewhat like our Northland salmon
scenes.place: Somewhat like our Northland salmon
scenes.reentry: From the blue-sea’s deepest caverns.”

scenes.title: In his belt the ancient hero
scenes.place: In his belt the ancient hero
scenes.reentry: Wore a knife insheathed with silver; From its case he drew the fish-knife,

scenes.title: Thus to carve the fish in pieces,
scenes.place: Thus to carve the fish in pieces,
scenes.reentry: Dress the nameless fish for roasting, Make of it a dainty breakfast,

scenes.title: Make of it a meal at noon-day,
scenes.place: Make of it a meal at noon-day,
scenes.reentry: Make for him a toothsome supper, Make the later meal at evening.

scenes.title: Straightway as the fish he touches,
scenes.place: Straightway as the fish he touches,
scenes.reentry: Touches with his knife of silver, Quick it leaps upon the waters,

scenes.title: Dives beneath the sea’s smooth surface,
scenes.place: Dives beneath the sea’s smooth surface,
scenes.reentry: From the boat with copper bottom, From the skiff of Wainamoinen.

scenes.title: In the waves at goodly distance,
scenes.place: In the waves at goodly distance,
scenes.reentry: Quickly from the sea it rises On the sixth and seventh billows,

scenes.title: Lifts its head above the waters,
scenes.place: Lifts its head above the waters,
scenes.reentry: Out of reach of fishing-tackle, Then addresses Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Chiding thus the ancient hero:
scenes.place: Chiding thus the ancient hero:
scenes.reentry: “Wainamoinen, ancient minstrel, Do not think that I came hither

scenes.title: To be fished for as a salmon,
scenes.place: To be fished for as a salmon,
scenes.reentry: Only to be chopped in pieces, Dressed and eaten like a whiting

scenes.title: Make for thee a dainty breakfast,
scenes.place: Make for thee a dainty breakfast,
scenes.reentry: Make for thee a meal at midday, Make for thee a toothsome supper,

scenes.title: Make the fourth meal of the Northland.”
scenes.place: Make the fourth meal of the Northland.”
scenes.reentry: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen: “Wherefore didst thou then come hither,

scenes.title: If it be not for my dinner?”
scenes.place: If it be not for my dinner?”
scenes.reentry: Thus the nameless fish made answer: “Hither have I come, O minstrel,

scenes.title: In thine arms to rest and linger,
scenes.place: In thine arms to rest and linger,
scenes.reentry: And thyself to love and cherish, At thy side a life-companion,

scenes.title: And thy wife to be forever;
scenes.place: And thy wife to be forever;
scenes.reentry: Deck thy couch with snowy linen, Smooth thy head upon the pillow,

scenes.title: Sweep thy rooms and make them cheery,
scenes.place: Sweep thy rooms and make them cheery,
scenes.reentry: Keep thy dwelling-place in order, Build a fire for thee when needed,

scenes.title: Bake for thee the honey-biscuit,
scenes.place: Bake for thee the honey-biscuit,
scenes.reentry: Fill thy cup with barley-water, Do for thee whatever pleases.

scenes.title: Not a trout of Northland rivers,
scenes.place: Not a trout of Northland rivers,
scenes.reentry: Not a whiting from the waters, Not a salmon of the North-seas,

scenes.title: I, a young and merry maiden,
scenes.place: I, a young and merry maiden,
scenes.reentry: Friend and sister of the fishes, Youkahainen’s youngest sister,

scenes.title: I, the one that thou dost fish for,
scenes.place: I, the one that thou dost fish for,
scenes.reentry: I am Aino whom thou lovest.

scenes.title: Now the foolish Wainamoinen,
scenes.place: Now the foolish Wainamoinen,
scenes.reentry: Scant of insight, scant of judgment, Didst not know enough to keep me,

scenes.title: Cruel-hearted, bloody-handed,
scenes.place: Cruel-hearted, bloody-handed,
scenes.reentry: Tried to kill me with thy fish-knife, So to roast me for thy dinner;

scenes.title: I, a mermaid of Wellamo,
scenes.place: I, a mermaid of Wellamo,
scenes.reentry: Once the fair and lovely Aino, Sister dear of Youkahainen.”

scenes.title: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen:,
scenes.place: Spake the ancient Wainamoinen:,
scenes.reentry: Filled with sorrow, much regretting: “Since thou’rt Youkahainen’s sister,

scenes.title: Beauteous Aino of Pohyola,
scenes.place: Beauteous Aino of Pohyola,
scenes.reentry: Come to me again I pray thee!”

scenes.title: Thus the mermaid wisely answered:
scenes.place: Thus the mermaid wisely answered:
scenes.reentry: “Nevermore will Aino’s spirit Fly to thee and be ill-treated.”

scenes.title: Quickly dived the water-maiden
scenes.place: Quickly dived the water-maiden
scenes.reentry: From the surface of the billow To the many-colored pebbles,

scenes.title: To the rainbow-tinted grottoes
scenes.place: To the rainbow-tinted grottoes
scenes.reentry: Where the mermaids live and linger.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, not discouraged,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, not discouraged,
scenes.reentry: Thought afresh and well reflected, How to live, and work, and win her;

scenes.title: Drew with care his silken fish-net,
scenes.place: Drew with care his silken fish-net,
scenes.reentry: To and fro through foam and billow, Through the bays and winding channels,

scenes.title: Drew it through the placid waters,
scenes.place: Drew it through the placid waters,
scenes.reentry: Drew it through the salmon-dwellings, Through the homes of water-maidens,

scenes.title: Through the waters of Wainola,
scenes.place: Through the waters of Wainola,
scenes.reentry: Through the blue-back of the ocean, Through the lakes of distant Lapland,

scenes.title: Through the rivers of Youkola,
scenes.place: Through the rivers of Youkola,
scenes.reentry: Through the seas of Kalevala, Hoping thus to find his Aino.

scenes.title: Many were the fish he landed,
scenes.place: Many were the fish he landed,
scenes.reentry: Every form of fish-like creatures, But he did not catch the sea-maid,

scenes.title: Not Wellamo’s water-maiden,
scenes.place: Not Wellamo’s water-maiden,
scenes.reentry: Fairest daughter of the Northland.

scenes.title: Finally the ancient minstrel,
scenes.place: Finally the ancient minstrel,
scenes.reentry: Mind depressed, and heart discouraged, Spake these words, immersed in sorrow: “Fool am I, and great my folly,

scenes.title: Having neither wit nor judgment;
scenes.place: Having neither wit nor judgment;
scenes.reentry: Surely once I had some knowledge, Had some insight into wisdom,

scenes.title: Had at least a bit of instinct;
scenes.place: Had at least a bit of instinct;
scenes.reentry: But my virtues all have left me In these mournful days of evil,

scenes.title: Vanished with my youth and vigor,
scenes.place: Vanished with my youth and vigor,
scenes.reentry: Insight gone, and sense departed, All my prudence gone to others!

scenes.title: Aino, whom I love and cherish,
scenes.place: Aino, whom I love and cherish,
scenes.reentry: All these years have sought to honor, Aino, now Wellamo’s maiden,

scenes.title: Promised friend of mine when needed,
scenes.place: Promised friend of mine when needed,
scenes.reentry: Promised bride of mine forever, Once I had within my power,

scenes.title: Caught her in Wellamo’s grottoes,
scenes.place: Caught her in Wellamo’s grottoes,
scenes.reentry: Led her to my boat of copper, With my fish-line made of silver;

scenes.title: But alas! I could not keep her,
scenes.place: But alas! I could not keep her,
scenes.reentry: Did not know that I had caught her Till too late to woo and win her;

scenes.title: Let her slip between my fingers
scenes.place: Let her slip between my fingers
scenes.reentry: To the home of water-maidens, To the kingdom of Wellamo.”

scenes.title: Wainamoinen then departed,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen then departed,
scenes.reentry: Empty-handed, heavy-hearted, Straightway hastened to his country,

scenes.title: To his home in Kalevala,
scenes.place: To his home in Kalevala,
scenes.reentry: Spake these words upon his journey: “What has happened to the cuckoo,

scenes.title: Once the cuckoo bringing gladness,
scenes.place: Once the cuckoo bringing gladness,
scenes.reentry: In the morning, in the evening, Often bringing joy at noontide?

scenes.title: What has stilled the cuckoo’s singing,
scenes.place: What has stilled the cuckoo’s singing,
scenes.reentry: What has changed the cuckoo’s calling? Sorrow must have stilled his singing,

scenes.title: And compassion changed his calling,
scenes.place: And compassion changed his calling,
scenes.reentry: As I hear him sing no longer, For my pleasure in the morning,

scenes.title: For my happiness at evening
scenes.place: For my happiness at evening
scenes.reentry: Never shall I learn the secret, How to live and how to prosper,

scenes.title: How upon the earth to rest me,
scenes.place: How upon the earth to rest me,
scenes.reentry: How upon the seas to wander! Only were my ancient mother

scenes.title: Living on the face of Northland,
scenes.place: Living on the face of Northland,
scenes.reentry: Surely she would well advise me, What my thought and what my action,

scenes.title: That this cup of grief might pass me,
scenes.place: That this cup of grief might pass me,
scenes.reentry: That this sorrow might escape me, And this darkened cloud pass over.”

scenes.title: In the deep awoke his mother,
scenes.place: In the deep awoke his mother,
scenes.reentry: From her tomb she spake as follows: “Only sleeping was thy mother,

scenes.title: Now awakes to give thee answer,
scenes.place: Now awakes to give thee answer,
scenes.reentry: What thy thought and what thine action, That this cup of grief may pass thee,

scenes.title: That this sorrow may escape thee,
scenes.place: That this sorrow may escape thee,
scenes.reentry: And this darkened cloud pass over. Hie thee straightway to the Northland,

scenes.title: Visit thou the Suomi daughters;
scenes.place: Visit thou the Suomi daughters;
scenes.reentry: Thou wilt find them wise and lovely, Far more beautiful than Aino,

scenes.title: Far more worthy of a husband,
scenes.place: Far more worthy of a husband,
scenes.reentry: Not such silly chatter-boxes, As the fickle Lapland maidens.

scenes.title: Take for thee a life-companion,
scenes.place: Take for thee a life-companion,
scenes.reentry: From the honest homes of Suomi, One of Northland’s honest daughters;

scenes.title: She will charm thee with her sweetness,
scenes.place: She will charm thee with her sweetness,
scenes.reentry: Make thee happy through her goodness, Form perfection, manners easy,

scenes.title: Every step and movement graceful,
scenes.place: Every step and movement graceful,
scenes.reentry: Full of wit and good behavior, Honor to thy home and kindred.”

scenes.title: Rune Vi
scenes.place: Rune Vi
scenes.reentry: Wainamoinen’S Hapless Journey.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, old and truthful,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, old and truthful,
scenes.reentry: Now arranges for a journey To the village of the Northland,

scenes.title: To the land of cruel winters,
scenes.place: To the land of cruel winters,
scenes.reentry: To the land of little sunshine, To the land of worthy women;

scenes.title: Takes his light-foot, royal racer,
scenes.place: Takes his light-foot, royal racer,
scenes.reentry: Then adjusts the golden bridle, Lays upon his back the saddle,

scenes.title: Silver-buckled, copper-stirruped,
scenes.place: Silver-buckled, copper-stirruped,
scenes.reentry: Seats himself upon his courser, And begins his journey northward;

scenes.title: Plunges onward, onward, onward,
scenes.place: Plunges onward, onward, onward,
scenes.reentry: Galloping along the highway, In his saddle, gaily fashioned,

scenes.title: On his dappled steed of magic,
scenes.place: On his dappled steed of magic,
scenes.reentry: Plunging through Wainola’s meadows, O’er the plains of Kalevala.

scenes.title: Fast and far he galloped onward,
scenes.place: Fast and far he galloped onward,
scenes.reentry: Galloped far beyond Wainola, Bounded o’er the waste of waters,

scenes.title: Till he reached the blue-sea’s margin,
scenes.place: Till he reached the blue-sea’s margin,
scenes.reentry: Wetting not the hoofs in running.

scenes.title: But the evil Youkahainen
scenes.place: But the evil Youkahainen
scenes.reentry: Nursed a grudge within his bosom, In his heart the worm of envy,

scenes.title: Envy of this Wainamoinen,
scenes.place: Envy of this Wainamoinen,
scenes.reentry: Of this wonderful enchanter. He prepares a cruel cross-bow,

scenes.title: Made of steel and other metals,
scenes.place: Made of steel and other metals,
scenes.reentry: Paints the bow in many colors, Molds the top-piece out of copper,

scenes.title: Trims his bow with snowy silver,
scenes.place: Trims his bow with snowy silver,
scenes.reentry: Gold he uses too in trimming. Then he hunts for strongest sinews,

scenes.title: Finds them in the stag of Hisi,
scenes.place: Finds them in the stag of Hisi,
scenes.reentry: Interweaves the flax of Lempo. Ready is the cruel cross-bow,

scenes.title: String, and shaft, and ends are finished,
scenes.place: String, and shaft, and ends are finished,
scenes.reentry: Beautiful the bow and mighty, Surely cost it not a trifle;

scenes.title: On the back a painted courser,
scenes.place: On the back a painted courser,
scenes.reentry: On each end a colt of beauty, Near the curve a maiden sleeping,

scenes.title: Near the notch a hare is bounding,
scenes.place: Near the notch a hare is bounding,
scenes.reentry: Wonderful the bow thus fashioned; Cuts some arrows for his quiver,

scenes.title: Covers them with finest feathers,
scenes.place: Covers them with finest feathers,
scenes.reentry: From the oak the shafts he fashions, Makes the tips of keenest metal.

scenes.title: As the rods and points are finished,
scenes.place: As the rods and points are finished,
scenes.reentry: Then he feathers well his arrows From the plumage of the swallow,

scenes.title: From the wing-quills of the sparrow;
scenes.place: From the wing-quills of the sparrow;
scenes.reentry: Hardens well his feathered arrows, And imparts to each new virtues,

scenes.title: Steeps them in the blood of serpents,
scenes.place: Steeps them in the blood of serpents,
scenes.reentry: In the virus of the adder.

scenes.title: Ready now are all his arrows,
scenes.place: Ready now are all his arrows,
scenes.reentry: Ready strung, his cruel cross-bow, Waiting for wise Wainamoinen.

scenes.title: Youkahainen, Lapland’s minstrel,
scenes.place: Youkahainen, Lapland’s minstrel,
scenes.reentry: Waits a long time, is not weary, Hopes to spy the ancient singer;

scenes.title: Spies at day-dawn, spies at evening,
scenes.place: Spies at day-dawn, spies at evening,
scenes.reentry: Spies he ceaselessly at noontide, Lies in wait for the magician,

scenes.title: Waits, and watches, as in envy;
scenes.place: Waits, and watches, as in envy;
scenes.reentry: Sits he at the open window, Stands behind the hedge, and watches;

scenes.title: In the foot-path waits, and listens,
scenes.place: In the foot-path waits, and listens,
scenes.reentry: Spies along the balks of meadows; On his back he hangs his quiver,

scenes.title: In his quiver, feathered arrows
scenes.place: In his quiver, feathered arrows
scenes.reentry: Dipped in virus of the viper, On his arm the mighty cross-bow,

scenes.title: Waits, and watches, and unwearied,
scenes.place: Waits, and watches, and unwearied,
scenes.reentry: Listens from the boat-house window, Lingers at the end of Fog-point,

scenes.title: By the river flowing seaward,
scenes.place: By the river flowing seaward,
scenes.reentry: Near the holy stream and whirlpool, Near the sacred river’s fire-fall.

scenes.title: Finally the Lapland minstrel,
scenes.place: Finally the Lapland minstrel,
scenes.reentry: Youkahainen of Pohyola, At the breaking of the day-dawn,

scenes.title: At the early hour of morning,
scenes.place: At the early hour of morning,
scenes.reentry: Fixed his gaze upon the North-east, Turned his eyes upon the sunrise,

scenes.title: Saw a black cloud on the ocean,
scenes.place: Saw a black cloud on the ocean,
scenes.reentry: Something blue upon the waters, And soliloquized as follows: “Are those clouds on the horizon,

scenes.title: Or perchance the dawn of morning?
scenes.place: Or perchance the dawn of morning?
scenes.reentry: Neither clouds on the horizon, Nor the dawning of the morning;

scenes.title: It is ancient Wainamoinen,
scenes.place: It is ancient Wainamoinen,
scenes.reentry: The renowned and wise enchanter, Riding on his way to Northland;

scenes.title: On his steed, the royal racer,
scenes.place: On his steed, the royal racer,
scenes.reentry: Magic courser of Wainola.”

scenes.title: Quickly now young Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Quickly now young Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Lapland’s vain and evil minstrel, Filled with envy, grasps his cross-bow,

scenes.title: Makes his bow and arrows ready
scenes.place: Makes his bow and arrows ready
scenes.reentry: For the death of Wainamoinen.

scenes.title: Quick his aged mother asked him,
scenes.place: Quick his aged mother asked him,
scenes.reentry: Spake these words to Youkahainen: “For whose slaughter is thy cross-bow,

scenes.title: For whose heart thy poisoned arrows?”
scenes.place: For whose heart thy poisoned arrows?”
scenes.reentry: Youkahainen thus made answer: “I have made this mighty cross-bow,

scenes.title: Fashioned bow and poisoned arrows
scenes.place: Fashioned bow and poisoned arrows
scenes.reentry: For the death of Wainamoinen, Thus to slay the friend of waters;

scenes.title: I must shoot the old magician,
scenes.place: I must shoot the old magician,
scenes.reentry: The eternal bard and hero, Through the heart, and through the liver,

scenes.title: Through the head, and through the shoulders,
scenes.place: Through the head, and through the shoulders,
scenes.reentry: With this bow and feathered arrows Thus destroy my rival minstrel.”

scenes.title: Then the aged mother answered,
scenes.place: Then the aged mother answered,
scenes.reentry: Thus reproving, thus forbidding: “Do not slay good Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Ancient hero of the Northland,
scenes.place: Ancient hero of the Northland,
scenes.reentry: From a noble tribe descended, He, my sister’s son, my nephew.

scenes.title: If thou slayest Wainamoinen,
scenes.place: If thou slayest Wainamoinen,
scenes.reentry: Ancient son of Kalevala, Then alas! all joy will vanish,

scenes.title: Perish all our wondrous singing;
scenes.place: Perish all our wondrous singing;
scenes.reentry: Better on the earth the gladness, Better here the magic music,

scenes.title: Than within the nether regions,
scenes.place: Than within the nether regions,
scenes.reentry: In the kingdom of Tuoni, In the realm of the departed,

scenes.title: In the land of the hereafter.”
scenes.place: In the land of the hereafter.”
scenes.reentry: Then the youthful Youkahainen

scenes.title: Thought awhile and well considered,
scenes.place: Thought awhile and well considered,
scenes.reentry: Ere he made a final answer.

scenes.title: With one hand he raised the cross-bow
scenes.place: With one hand he raised the cross-bow
scenes.reentry: But the other seemed to weaken, As he drew the cruel bow-string.

scenes.title: Finally these words he uttered
scenes.place: Finally these words he uttered
scenes.reentry: As his bosom swelled with envy: “Let all joy forever vanish,

scenes.title: Let earth’s pleasures quickly perish,
scenes.place: Let earth’s pleasures quickly perish,
scenes.reentry: Disappear earth’s sweetest music, Happiness depart forever;

scenes.title: Shoot I will this rival minstrel,
scenes.place: Shoot I will this rival minstrel,
scenes.reentry: Little heeding what the end is.”

scenes.title: Quickly now he bends his fire-bow,
scenes.place: Quickly now he bends his fire-bow,
scenes.reentry: On his left knee rests the weapon, With his right foot firmly planted,

scenes.title: Thus he strings his bow of envy;
scenes.place: Thus he strings his bow of envy;
scenes.reentry: Takes three arrows from his quiver, Choosing well the best among them,

scenes.title: Carefully adjusts the bow-string,
scenes.place: Carefully adjusts the bow-string,
scenes.reentry: Sets with care the feathered arrow, To the flaxen string he lays it,

scenes.title: Holds the cross-bow to his shoulder,
scenes.place: Holds the cross-bow to his shoulder,
scenes.reentry: Aiming well along the margin, At the heart of Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Waiting till he gallops nearer;
scenes.place: Waiting till he gallops nearer;
scenes.reentry: In the shadow of a thicket, Speaks these words while he is waiting “Be thou, flaxen string, elastic;

scenes.title: Swiftly fly, thou feathered ash-wood,
scenes.place: Swiftly fly, thou feathered ash-wood,
scenes.reentry: Swiftly speed, thou deadly missile, Quick as light, thou poisoned arrow,

scenes.title: To the heart of Wainamoinen
scenes.place: To the heart of Wainamoinen
scenes.reentry: If my hand too low should hold thee, May the gods direct thee higher;

scenes.title: If too high mine eye should aim thee,
scenes.place: If too high mine eye should aim thee,
scenes.reentry: May the gods direct thee lower.”

scenes.title: Steady now he pulls the trigger;
scenes.place: Steady now he pulls the trigger;
scenes.reentry: Like the lightning flies the arrow O’er the head of Wainamoinen;

scenes.title: To the upper sky it darteth,
scenes.place: To the upper sky it darteth,
scenes.reentry: And the highest clouds it pierces, Scatters all the flock of lamb-clouds,

scenes.title: On its rapid journey skyward
scenes.place: On its rapid journey skyward
scenes.reentry: Not discouraged, quick selecting,

scenes.title: Quick adjusting, Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Quick adjusting, Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Quickly aiming, shoots a second. Speeds the arrow swift as lightning;

scenes.title: Much too low he aimed the missile,
scenes.place: Much too low he aimed the missile,
scenes.reentry: Into earth the arrow plunges, Pierces to the lower regions,

scenes.title: Splits in two the old Sand Mountain
scenes.place: Splits in two the old Sand Mountain
scenes.reentry: Nothing daunted, Youkahainen,

scenes.title: Quick adjusting shoots a third one
scenes.place: Quick adjusting shoots a third one
scenes.reentry: Swift as light it speeds its journey, Strikes the steed of Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Strikes the light-foot, ocean-swimmer,
scenes.place: Strikes the light-foot, ocean-swimmer,
scenes.reentry: Strikes him near his golden girdle, Through the shoulder of the racer.

scenes.title: Thereupon wise Wainamoinen
scenes.place: Thereupon wise Wainamoinen
scenes.reentry: Headlong fell upon the waters, Plunged beneath the rolling billows,

scenes.title: From the saddle of the courser,
scenes.place: From the saddle of the courser,
scenes.reentry: From his dappled steed of magic. Then arose a mighty storm-wind,

scenes.title: Roaring wildly on the waters,
scenes.place: Roaring wildly on the waters,
scenes.reentry: Bore away old Wainamoinen Far from land upon the billows,

scenes.title: On the high and rolling billows,
scenes.place: On the high and rolling billows,
scenes.reentry: On the broad sea’s great expanses.

scenes.title: Boasted then young Youkahainen,
scenes.place: Boasted then young Youkahainen,
scenes.reentry: Thinking Waino dead and buried, These the boastful words he uttered: “Nevermore, old Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Nevermore in all thy life-time,
scenes.place: Nevermore in all thy life-time,
scenes.reentry: While the golden moonlight glistens, Nevermore wilt fix thy vision

scenes.title: On the meadows of Wainola,
scenes.place: On the meadows of Wainola,
scenes.reentry: On the plains of Kalevala; Full six years must swim the ocean,

scenes.title: Tread the waves for seven summers,
scenes.place: Tread the waves for seven summers,
scenes.reentry: Eight years ride the foamy billows, In the broad expanse of water;

scenes.title: Six long autumns as a fir-tree,
scenes.place: Six long autumns as a fir-tree,
scenes.reentry: Seven winters as a pebble, Eight long summers as an aspen.”

scenes.title: Thereupon the Lapland minstrel
scenes.place: Thereupon the Lapland minstrel
scenes.reentry: Hastened to his room delighting, When his mother thus addressed him “Hast thou slain good Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Slain the son of Kalevala?”
scenes.place: Slain the son of Kalevala?”
scenes.reentry: Youkahainen thus made answer: “I have slain old Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Slain the son of Kalevala,
scenes.place: Slain the son of Kalevala,
scenes.reentry: That he now may plow the ocean, That he now may sweep the waters,

scenes.title: On the billows rock and slumber
scenes.place: On the billows rock and slumber
scenes.reentry: In the salt-sea plunged he headlong, In the deep sank the magician,

scenes.title: Sidewise turned he to the sea-shore,
scenes.place: Sidewise turned he to the sea-shore,
scenes.reentry: On his back to rock forever, Thus the boundless sea to travel,

scenes.title: Thus to ride the rolling billows.”
scenes.place: Thus to ride the rolling billows.”
scenes.reentry: This the answer of the mother: “Woe to earth for this thine action,

scenes.title: Gone forever, joy and singing,
scenes.place: Gone forever, joy and singing,
scenes.reentry: Vanished is the wit of ages! Thou hast slain good Wainamoinen,

scenes.title: Slain the ancient wisdom-singer,
scenes.place: Slain the ancient wisdom-singer,
scenes.reentry: Slain the pride of Suwantala, Slain the hero of Wainola,

scenes.title: Rune Vii
scenes.place: Rune Vii
scenes.reentry: Wainamoinen’S Rescue.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, old and truthful,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, old and truthful,
scenes.reentry: Swam through all the deep-sea waters, Floating like a branch of aspen,

scenes.title: Like a withered twig of willow;
scenes.place: Like a withered twig of willow;
scenes.reentry: Swam six days in summer weather, Swam six nights in golden moonlight;

scenes.title: Still before him rose the billows,
scenes.place: Still before him rose the billows,
scenes.reentry: And behind him sky and ocean. Two days more he swam undaunted,

scenes.title: Two long nights he struggled onward
scenes.place: Two long nights he struggled onward
scenes.reentry: On the evening of the eighth day, Wainamoinen grew disheartened,

scenes.title: Felt a very great discomfort,
scenes.place: Felt a very great discomfort,
scenes.reentry: For his feet had lost their toe-nails, And his fingers dead and dying.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, ancient minstrel,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, ancient minstrel,
scenes.reentry: Sad and weary, spake as follows: “Woe is me, my old life fated!

scenes.title: Woe is me, misfortune’s offspring!
scenes.place: Woe is me, misfortune’s offspring!
scenes.reentry: Fool was I when fortune favored, To forsake my home and kindred,

scenes.title: For a maiden fair and lovely,
scenes.place: For a maiden fair and lovely,
scenes.reentry: Here beneath the starry heavens, In this cruel waste of waters,

scenes.title: Days and nights to swim and wander,
scenes.place: Days and nights to swim and wander,
scenes.reentry: Here to struggle with the storm-winds, To be tossed by heaving billows,

scenes.title: In this broad sea’s great expanses,
scenes.place: In this broad sea’s great expanses,
scenes.reentry: In this ocean vast and boundless.

scenes.title: Painful too for me to linger
scenes.place: Painful too for me to linger
scenes.reentry: Evermore within these waters, Thus to struggle for existence!

scenes.title: Cannot know how I can prosper,
scenes.place: Cannot know how I can prosper,
scenes.reentry: How to find me food and shelter, In these cold and lifeless waters,

scenes.title: In these days of dire misfortune
scenes.place: In these days of dire misfortune
scenes.reentry: Build I in the winds my dwelling? It will find no sure foundation.

scenes.title: Build my home upon the billows?
scenes.place: Build my home upon the billows?
scenes.reentry: Surely would the waves destroy it.”

scenes.title: Comes a bird from far Pohyola,
scenes.place: Comes a bird from far Pohyola,
scenes.reentry: From the occident, an eagle, Is not classed among the largest,

scenes.title: Nor belongs he to the smallest;
scenes.place: Nor belongs he to the smallest;
scenes.reentry: One wing touches on the waters, While the other sweeps the heavens;

scenes.title: O’er the waves he wings his body,
scenes.place: O’er the waves he wings his body,
scenes.reentry: Strikes his beak upon the sea-cliffs, Flies about, then safely perches,

scenes.title: Looks before him, looks behind him,
scenes.place: Looks before him, looks behind him,
scenes.reentry: There beholds brave Wainamoinen, On the blue-back of the ocean,

scenes.title: And the eagle thus accosts him:
scenes.place: And the eagle thus accosts him:
scenes.reentry: “Wherefore art thou, ancient hero, Swimming in the deep-sea billows?”

scenes.title: Thus the water-minstrel answered:
scenes.place: Thus the water-minstrel answered:
scenes.reentry: “I am ancient Wainamoinen, Friend and fellow of the waters,

scenes.title: I, the famous wisdom-singer;
scenes.place: I, the famous wisdom-singer;
scenes.reentry: Went to woo a Northland maiden, Maiden from the dismal Darkland,

scenes.title: Quickly galloped on my journey,
scenes.place: Quickly galloped on my journey,
scenes.reentry: Riding on the plain of ocean. I arrived one morning early,

scenes.title: At the breaking of the day-dawn
scenes.place: At the breaking of the day-dawn
scenes.reentry: At the bay of Luotola, Near Youkola’s foaming river,

scenes.title: Where the evil Youkahainen
scenes.place: Where the evil Youkahainen
scenes.reentry: Slew my steed with bow and arrow, Tried to slay me with his weapons.

scenes.title: On the waters fell I headlong,
scenes.place: On the waters fell I headlong,
scenes.reentry: Plunged beneath the salt-sea’s surface, From the saddle of the courser,

scenes.title: From my dappled steed of magic
scenes.place: From my dappled steed of magic
scenes.reentry: “Then arose a mighty storm-wind,

scenes.title: From the East and West a whirlwind,
scenes.place: From the East and West a whirlwind,
scenes.reentry: Washed me seaward on the surges, Seaward, seaward, further, further,

scenes.title: Where for many days I wandered,
scenes.place: Where for many days I wandered,
scenes.reentry: Swam and rocked upon the billows, Where as many nights I struggled,

scenes.title: In the dashing waves and sea-foam,
scenes.place: In the dashing waves and sea-foam,
scenes.reentry: With the angry winds and waters.

scenes.title: Cannot solve this heavy problem,
scenes.place: Cannot solve this heavy problem,
scenes.reentry: How to live nor how to perish In this cruel salt-sea water.

scenes.title: Build I in the winds my dwelling?
scenes.place: Build I in the winds my dwelling?
scenes.reentry: It will find no sure foundation. Build my home upon the waters?

scenes.title: Surely will the waves destroy it
scenes.place: Surely will the waves destroy it
scenes.reentry: Must I swim the sea forever, Must I live, or must I perish?

scenes.title: What will happen if I perish,
scenes.place: What will happen if I perish,
scenes.reentry: If I sink below the billows, Perish here from cold and hunger?”

scenes.title: Thus the bird of Ether answered:
scenes.place: Thus the bird of Ether answered:
scenes.reentry: “Be not in the least disheartened, Place thyself between my shoulders,

scenes.title: On my back be firmly seated,
scenes.place: On my back be firmly seated,
scenes.reentry: I will lift thee from the waters, Bear thee with my pinions upward,

scenes.title: Bear thee wheresoe’er thou willest
scenes.place: Bear thee wheresoe’er thou willest
scenes.reentry: Well do I the day remember Where thou didst the eagle service,

scenes.title: When thou didst the birds a favor
scenes.place: When thou didst the birds a favor
scenes.reentry: Thou didst leave the birch-tree standing, When were cleared the Osmo-forests,

scenes.title: From the lands of Kalevala,
scenes.place: From the lands of Kalevala,
scenes.reentry: As a home for weary song-birds, As a resting-place for eagles.”

scenes.title: Then arises Wainamoinen,
scenes.place: Then arises Wainamoinen,
scenes.reentry: Lifts his head above the waters, Boldly rises from the sea-waves,

scenes.title: Lifts his body from the billows,
scenes.place: Lifts his body from the billows,
scenes.reentry: Seats himself upon the eagle, On the eagle’s feathered shoulders.

scenes.title: Quick aloft the huge bird bears him,
scenes.place: Quick aloft the huge bird bears him,
scenes.reentry: Bears the ancient Wainamoinen, Bears him on the path of zephyrs,

scenes.title: Floating on the vernal breezes,
scenes.place: Floating on the vernal breezes,
scenes.reentry: To the distant shore of Northland, To the dismal Sariola,

scenes.title: Where the eagle leaves his burden,
scenes.place: Where the eagle leaves his burden,
scenes.reentry: Flies away to join his fellows.

scenes.title: Wainamoinen, lone and weary,
scenes.place: Wainamoinen, lone and weary,
scenes.reentry: Straightway fell to bitter weeping, Wept and moaned in heavy accents,

scenes.title: On the border of the blue-sea,
scenes.place: On the border of the blue-sea,
scenes.reentry: On a cheerless promontory, With a hundred wounds tormented,

scenes.title: Made by cruel winds and waters,
scenes.place: Made by cruel winds and waters,
scenes.reentry: With his hair and beard dishevelled By the surging of the billows.

scenes.title: Three long days he wept disheartened
scenes.place: Three long days he wept disheartened
scenes.reentry: Wept as many nights in anguish, Did not know what way to journey,

scenes.title: Could not find a woodland foot-print,
scenes.place: Could not find a woodland foot-print,
scenes.reentry: That would point him to the highway, To his home in Kalevala,

scenes.title: To his much-loved home and kindred
scenes.place: To his much-loved home and kindred
scenes.reentry: Northland’s young and slender maiden,

scenes.title: With complexion fair and lovely,
scenes.place: With complexion fair and lovely,
scenes.reentry: With the Sun had laid a wager, With the Sun and Moon a wager,

scenes.title: Which should rise before the other,
scenes.place: Which should rise before the other,
scenes.reentry: On the morning of the morrow. And the maiden rose in beauty,

scenes.title: Long before the Sun had risen,
scenes.place: Long before the Sun had risen,
scenes.reentry: Long before the Moon had wakened, From their beds beneath the ocean.

scenes.title: Ere the cock had crowed the day-break,
scenes.place: Ere the cock had crowed the day-break,
scenes.reentry: Ere the Sun had broken slumber; She had sheared six gentle lambkins,

scenes.title: Gathered from them six white fleeces,
scenes.place: Gathered from them six white fleeces,
scenes.reentry: Hence to make the rolls for spinning, Hence to form the threads for weaving,

scenes.title: Hence to make the softest raiment,
scenes.place: Hence to make the softest raiment,
scenes.reentry: Ere the morning dawn had broken, Ere the sleeping Sun had risen.

scenes.title: When this task the maid had ended,
scenes.place: When this task the maid had ended,
scenes.reentry: Then she scrubbed the birchen tables, Sweeps the ground-floor of the stable,

scenes.title: With a broom of leaves and branches
scenes.place: With a broom of leaves and branches
scenes.reentry: From the birches of the Northland, Scrapes the sweepings well together

scenes.title: On a shovel made of copper,
scenes.place: On a shovel made of copper,
scenes.reentry: Carries them beyond the stable, From the doorway to the meadow,

scenes.title: To the meadow’s distant border,
scenes.place: To the meadow’s distant border,
scenes.reentry: Near the surges of the great-sea, Listens there and looks about her,

scenes.title: Hears a wailing from the waters,
scenes.place: Hears a wailing from the waters,
scenes.reentry: Hears a weeping from the sea-shore, Hears a hero-voice lamenting.

scenes.title: Thereupon she hastens homeward,
scenes.place: Thereupon she hastens homeward,
scenes.reentry: Hastens to her mother’s dwelling, These the words the maiden utters: “I have heard a wail from ocean,

scenes.title: Heard a weeping from the sea-coast,
scenes.place: Heard a weeping from the sea-coast,
scenes.reentry: On the shore some one lamenting.”

scenes.title: Louhi, hostess of Pohyola,
scenes.place: Louhi, hostess of Pohyola,
scenes.reentry: Ancient, toothless dame of Northland, Hastens from her door and court-yard,

scenes.title: Through the meadow to the sea-shore,
scenes.place: Through the meadow to the sea-shore,
scenes.reentry: Listens well for sounds of weeping, For the wail of one in sorrow;

scenes.title: Hears the voice of one in trouble,
scenes.place: Hears the voice of one in trouble,
scenes.reentry: Hears a hero-cry of anguish. Thus the ancient Louhi answers: “This is not the wail of children,

scenes.title: These are not the tears of women,
scenes.place: These are not the tears of women,
scenes.reentry: In this way weep bearded heroes; This the hero-cry of anguish.”

scenes.title: Quick she pushed her boat to water,
scenes.place: Quick she pushed her boat to water,
scenes.reentry: To the floods her goodly vessel, Straightway rows with lightning swiftness,

scenes.title: To the weeping Wainamoinen;
scenes.place: To the weeping Wainamoinen;
scenes.reentry: Gives the hero consolation, Comfort gives she to the minstrel

scenes.title: Wailing in a grove of willows,
scenes.place: Wailing in a grove of willows,
scenes.reentry: In his piteous condition, Mid the alder-trees and aspens,

scenes.title: On the border of the salt-sea,
scenes.place: On the border of the salt-sea,
scenes.reentry: Visage trembling, locks dishevelled, Ears, and eyes, and lips of sadness.

scenes.title: Louhi, hostess of Pohyola,
scenes.place: Louhi, hostess of Pohyola,
scenes.reentry: Thus addresses Wainamoinen: “Tell me what has been thy folly,

scenes.title: That thou art in this condition.”
scenes.place: That thou art in this condition.”
scenes.reentry: Old and truthful Wainamoinen

scenes.title: Lifts aloft his head and answers:
scenes.place: Lifts aloft his head and answers:
scenes.reentry: “Well I know that it is folly That has brought me all this trouble,

scenes.title: Brought me to this land of strangers,
scenes.place: Brought me to this land of strangers,
scenes.reentry: To these regions unbefitting; Happy was I with my kindred,

scenes.title: In my distant home and country,
scenes.place: In my distant home and country,
scenes.reentry: There my name was named in honor.”

scenes.title: Louhi, hostess of Pohyola,
scenes.place: Louhi, hostess of Pohyola,
scenes.reentry: Thus replied to Wainamoinen: “I would gain the information,

scenes.title: Should I be allowed to ask thee,
scenes.place: Should I be allowed to ask thee,
scenes.reentry: Who thou art of ancient heroes, Who of all the host of heroes?”

scenes.title: This is Wainamoinen’s answer:
scenes.place: This is Wainamoinen’s answer:
scenes.reentry: “Formerly my name was mentioned, Often was I heard and honored,

scenes.title: As a minstrel and magician,
scenes.place: As a minstrel and magician,
scenes.reentry: In the long and dreary winters, Called the Singer of the Northland,

scenes.title: In the valleys of Wainola,
scenes.place: In the valleys of Wainola,
scenes.reentry: On the plains of Kalevala; No one thought that such misfortune

scenes.title: Could befall wise Wainamoinen.”
scenes.place: Could befall wise Wainamoinen.”
scenes.reentry: Louhi, hostess of Pohyola,

scenes.title: Thus replied in cheering accents:
scenes.place: Thus replied in cheering accents:
scenes.reentry: “Rise, O hero, from discomfort, From thy bed among the willows;

scenes.title: Enter now upon the new-way,
scenes.place: Enter now upon the new-way,
scenes.reentry: Come with me to yonder dwelling, There relate thy strange adventures,

scenes.title: Tell the tale of thy misfortunes.”
scenes.place: Tell the tale of thy misfortunes.”
scenes.reentry: Now she takes the hapless hero,

scenes.title: Lifts him from his bed of sorrow,

scenes.title: Bringing also golden goblets;
scenes.place: Bringing also golden goblets;
scenes.reentry: Dip they up a very little, But the very smallest measure

scenes.title: Of the blood of the magician,
scenes.place: Of the blood of the magician,
scenes.reentry: From the wounds of Wainamoinen.

scenes.title: From the fire-place calls the old man,
scenes.place: From the fire-place calls the old man,
scenes.reentry: Thus the gray-beard asks the minstrel: “Tell me who thou art of heroes,

scenes.title: Who of all the great magicians?
scenes.place: Who of all the great magicians?
scenes.reentry: Lo! thy blood fills seven sea-boats, Eight of largest birchen vessels,

scenes.title: Flowing from some hero’s veinlets,
scenes.place: Flowing from some hero’s veinlets,
scenes.reentry: From the wounds of some magician. Other matters I would ask thee;

scenes.title: Sing the cause of this thy trouble,
scenes.place: Sing the cause of this thy trouble,
scenes.reentry: Sing to me the source of metals, Sing the origin of iron,

scenes.title: How at first it was created.”
scenes.place: How at first it was created.”
scenes.reentry: Then the ancient Wainamoinen

scenes.title: Made this answer to the gray-beard:
scenes.place: Made this answer to the gray-beard:
scenes.reentry: “Know I well the source of metals, Know the origin of iron;

scenes.title: I can tell bow steel is fashioned
scenes.place: I can tell bow steel is fashioned
scenes.reentry: Of the mothers air is oldest, Water is the oldest brother,

scenes.title: And the fire is second brother,
scenes.place: And the fire is second brother,
scenes.reentry: And the youngest brother, iron; Ukko is the first creator.

scenes.title: Ukko, maker of the heavens,
scenes.place: Ukko, maker of the heavens,
scenes.reentry: Cut apart the air and water, Ere was born the metal, iron.

scenes.title: Ukko, maker of the heavens,
scenes.place: Ukko, maker of the heavens,
scenes.reentry: Firmly rubbed his hands together, Firmly pressed them on his knee-cap,

scenes.title: Then arose three lovely maidens,
scenes.place: Then arose three lovely maidens,
scenes.reentry: Three most beautiful of daughters; These were mothers of the iron,

scenes.title: And of steel of bright-blue color
scenes.place: And of steel of bright-blue color
scenes.reentry: Tremblingly they walked the heavens, Walked the clouds with silver linings,

scenes.title: With their bosoms overflowing
scenes.place: With their bosoms overflowing
scenes.reentry: With the milk of future iron, Flowing on and flowing ever,

scenes.title: From the bright rims of the cloudlets
scenes.place: From the bright rims of the cloudlets
scenes.reentry: To the earth, the valleys filling, To the slumber-calling waters.

scenes.title: Black milk over river channels
scenes.place: Black milk over river channels
scenes.reentry: And the second daughter sprinkled White milk over hills and mountains,

scenes.title: While the youngest daughter sprinkled
scenes.place: While the youngest daughter sprinkled
scenes.reentry: Red milk over seas and oceans. Where the black milk had been sprinked,

scenes.title: Grew the dark and ductile iron;
scenes.place: Grew the dark and ductile iron;
scenes.reentry: Where the white milk had been sprinkled, Grew the iron, lighter-colored;

scenes.title: Where the red milk had been sprinkled,
scenes.place: Where the red milk had been sprinkled,
scenes.reentry: Grew the red and brittle iron.

scenes.title: Iron hastened Fire to visit,
scenes.place: Iron hastened Fire to visit,
scenes.reentry: His beloved elder brother, Thus to know his brother better.

scenes.title: Straightway Fire began his roarings,
scenes.place: Straightway Fire began his roarings,
scenes.reentry: Labored to consume his brother, His beloved younger brother.

scenes.title: Straightway Iron sees his danger,
scenes.place: Straightway Iron sees his danger,
scenes.reentry: Saves himself by fleetly fleeing, From the fiery flame’s advances,

scenes.title: Fleeing hither, fleeing thither,
scenes.place: Fleeing hither, fleeing thither,
scenes.reentry: Fleeing still and taking shelter In the swamps and in the valleys,

scenes.title: In the springs that loudly bubble,
scenes.place: In the springs that loudly bubble,
scenes.reentry: By the rivers winding seaward, On the broad backs of the marshes,

scenes.title: Where the swans their nests have builded,
scenes.place: Where the swans their nests have builded,
scenes.reentry: Where the wild geese hatch their goslings.

scenes.title: Stretching by the water-courses,
scenes.place: Stretching by the water-courses,
scenes.reentry: Hidden well for many ages, Hidden in the birchen forests,

scenes.title: But he could not hide forever
scenes.place: But he could not hide forever
scenes.reentry: From the searchings of his brother; Here and there the fire has caught him,

scenes.title: Caught and brought him to his furnace,
scenes.place: Caught and brought him to his furnace,
scenes.reentry: That the spears, and swords, and axes, Might be forged and duly hammered.

scenes.title: In the swamps ran blackened waters,
scenes.place: In the swamps ran blackened waters,
scenes.reentry: From the heath the bears came ambling, And the wolves ran through the marshes.

scenes.title: Iron then made his appearance,
scenes.place: Iron then made his appearance,
scenes.reentry: Where the feet of wolves had trodden, Where the paws of bears had trampled.

scenes.title: Came to earth to work the metal;
scenes.place: Came to earth to work the metal;
scenes.reentry: He was born upon the Coal-mount, Skilled and nurtured in the coal-fields;

scenes.title: In one hand, a copper hammer,
scenes.place: In one hand, a copper hammer,
scenes.reentry: In the other, tongs of iron; In the night was born the blacksmith,

scenes.title: In the morn he built his smithy,
scenes.place: In the morn he built his smithy,
scenes.reentry: Sought with care a favored hillock, Where the winds might fill his bellows;

scenes.title: Found a hillock in the swamp-lands,
scenes.place: Found a hillock in the swamp-lands,
scenes.reentry: Where the iron hid abundant; There he built his smelting furnace,

scenes.title: There he laid his leathern bellows,
scenes.place: There he laid his leathern bellows,
scenes.reentry: Hastened where the wolves had travelled, Followed where the bears had trampled,

scenes.title: Found the iron’s young formations,
scenes.place: Found the iron’s young formations,
scenes.reentry: In the wolf-tracks of the marshes, In the foot-prints of the gray-bear.

scenes.title: Thus addressed the sleeping iron:
scenes.place: Thus addressed the sleeping iron:
scenes.reentry: ‘Thou most useful of the metals, Thou art sleeping in the marshes,

scenes.title: Thou art hid in low conditions,
scenes.place: Thou art hid in low conditions,
scenes.reentry: Where the wolf treads in the swamp-lands, Where the bear sleeps in the thickets.

scenes.title: Hast thou thought and well considered,
scenes.place: Hast thou thought and well considered,
scenes.reentry: What would be thy future station, Should I place thee in the furnace,

scenes.title: Thus to make thee free and useful?’
scenes.place: Thus to make thee free and useful?’
scenes.reentry: “Then was Iron sorely frightened,

scenes.title: Much distressed and filled with horror,
scenes.place: Much distressed and filled with horror,
scenes.reentry: When of Fire he heard the mention, Mention of his fell destroyer.

scenes.title: Thus the smith addresses Iron:
scenes.place: Thus the smith addresses Iron:
scenes.reentry: ‘Be not frightened, useful metal, Surely Fire will not consume thee,

scenes.title: Will not burn his youngest brother,
scenes.place: Will not burn his youngest brother,
scenes.reentry: Will not harm his nearest kindred. Come thou to my room and furnace,

scenes.title: Where the fire is freely burning,
scenes.place: Where the fire is freely burning,
scenes.reentry: Thou wilt live, and grow, and prosper, Wilt become the swords of heroes,

scenes.title: Buckles for the belts of women.’
scenes.place: Buckles for the belts of women.’
scenes.reentry: “Ere arose the star of evening,

scenes.title: Iron ore had left the marshes,
scenes.place: Iron ore had left the marshes,
scenes.reentry: From the water-beds had risen, Had been carried to the furnace,

scenes.title: In the fire the smith had laid it,
scenes.place: In the fire the smith had laid it,
scenes.reentry: Laid it in his smelting furnace. Ilmarinen starts the bellows,

scenes.title: Gives three motions of the handle,
scenes.place: Gives three motions of the handle,
scenes.reentry: And the iron flows in streamlets From the forge of the magician,

scenes.title: Soon becomes like baker’s leaven,
scenes.place: Soon becomes like baker’s leaven,
scenes.reentry: Soft as dough for bread of barley. Then out-screamed the metal, Iron: ‘Wondrous blacksmith, Ilmarinen,

scenes.title: Take, O take me from thy furnace,
scenes.place: Take, O take me from thy furnace,
scenes.reentry: From this fire and cruel torture.’

scenes.title: Thou art but a little frightened,
scenes.place: Thou art but a little frightened,
scenes.reentry: Thou shalt be a mighty power, Thou shalt slay the best of heroes,

scenes.title: Thou shalt wound thy dearest brother.’
scenes.place: Thou shalt wound thy dearest brother.’
scenes.reentry: “Straightway Iron made this promise,

scenes.title: Vowed and swore in strongest accents,
scenes.place: Vowed and swore in strongest accents,
scenes.reentry: By the furnace, by the anvil, By the tongs, and by the hammer,

scenes.title: These the words he vowed and uttered:
scenes.place: These the words he vowed and uttered:
scenes.reentry: ‘Many trees that I shall injure, Shall devour the hearts of mountains,

scenes.title: Shall not slay my nearest kindred,
scenes.place: Shall not slay my nearest kindred,
scenes.reentry: Shall not kill the best of heroes, Shall not wound my dearest brother;

scenes.title: Better live in civil freedom,
scenes.place: Better live in civil freedom,
scenes.reentry: Happier would be my life-time, Should I serve my fellow-beings,

scenes.title: Serve as tools for their convenience,
scenes.place: Serve as tools for their convenience,
scenes.reentry: Than as implements of warfare, Slay my friends and nearest kindred,

scenes.title: Wound the children of my mother.’
scenes.place: Wound the children of my mother.’
scenes.reentry: “Now the master, Ilmarinen,

scenes.title: The renowned and skilful blacksmith,
scenes.place: The renowned and skilful blacksmith,
scenes.reentry: From the fire removes the iron, Places it upon the anvil,

scenes.title: Hammers well until it softens,
scenes.place: Hammers well until it softens,
scenes.reentry: Hammers many fine utensils, Hammers spears, and swords, and axes,

scenes.title: Hammers knives, and forks, and hatchets,
scenes.place: Hammers knives, and forks, and hatchets,
scenes.reentry: Hammers tools of all descriptions.

scenes.title: Many things he could not fashion,
scenes.place: Many things he could not fashion,
scenes.reentry: Could not make the tongue of iron, Could not hammer steel from iron,

scenes.title: Could not make the iron harden
scenes.place: Could not make the iron harden
scenes.reentry: Well considered Ilmarinen, Deeply thought and long reflected.

scenes.title: Then he gathered birchen ashes,
scenes.place: Then he gathered birchen ashes,
scenes.reentry: Steeped the ashes in the water, Made a lye to harden iron,

scenes.title: Thus to form the steel most needful
scenes.place: Thus to form the steel most needful
scenes.reentry: With his tongue he tests the mixture, Weighs it long and well considers,

scenes.title: And the blacksmith speaks as follows:
scenes.place: And the blacksmith speaks as follows:
scenes.reentry: ‘All this labor is for nothing, Will not fashion steel from iron,

scenes.title: Will not make the soft ore harden.’
scenes.place: Will not make the soft ore harden.’
scenes.reentry: “Now a bee flies from the meadow,

scenes.title: Blue-wing coming from the flowers,
scenes.place: Blue-wing coming from the flowers,
scenes.reentry: Flies about, then safely settles Near the furnace of the smithy.

scenes.title: These the words of Ilmarinen:
scenes.place: These the words of Ilmarinen:
scenes.reentry: ‘Little bee, thou tiny birdling, Bring me honey on thy winglets,

scenes.title: On thy tongue, I pray thee, bring me
scenes.place: On thy tongue, I pray thee, bring me
scenes.reentry: Sweetness from the fragrant meadows, From the little cups of flowers,

scenes.title: From the tips of seven petals,
scenes.place: From the tips of seven petals,
scenes.reentry: That we thus may aid the water To produce the steel from iron.’

scenes.title: Heard these words of Ilmarinen,
scenes.place: Heard these words of Ilmarinen,
scenes.reentry: Looking from the cottage gable, Flying to the bark of birch-trees,

scenes.title: While the iron bars were heating,
scenes.place: While the iron bars were heating,
scenes.reentry: While the steel was being tempered; Swiftly flew the stinging hornet,

scenes.title: Scattered all the Hisi horrors,
scenes.place: Scattered all the Hisi horrors,
scenes.reentry: Brought the blessing of the serpent, Brought the venom of the adder,

scenes.title: Brought the poison of the spider,
scenes.place: Brought the poison of the spider,
scenes.reentry: Brought the stings of all the insects, Mixed them with the ore and water,

scenes.title: While the steel was being tempered
scenes.place: While the steel was being tempered
scenes.reentry: “Ilmarinen, skilful blacksmith,

scenes.title: First of all the iron-workers,
scenes.place: First of all the iron-workers,
scenes.reentry: Thought the bee had surely brought him Honey from the fragrant meadows,

scenes.title: From the little cups of flowers,
scenes.place: From the little cups of flowers,
scenes.reentry: From the tips of seven petals, And he spake the words that follow: ‘Welcome, welcome, is thy coming,

scenes.title: Honeyed sweetness from the flowers
scenes.place: Honeyed sweetness from the flowers
scenes.reentry: Thou hast brought to aid the water, Thus to form the steel from iron!’

scenes.title: Dipped the iron into water,
scenes.place: Dipped the iron into water,
scenes.reentry: Water mixed with many poisons, Thought it but the wild bee’s honey;

scenes.title: Thus he formed the steel from iron
scenes.place: Thus he formed the steel from iron
scenes.reentry: When he plunged it into water, Water mixed with many poisons,

scenes.title: When he placed it in the furnace,
scenes.place: When he placed it in the furnace,
scenes.reentry: Angry grew the hardened iron, Broke the vow that he had taken,

scenes.title: Ate his words like dogs and devils,
scenes.place: Ate his words like dogs and devils,
scenes.reentry: Mercilessly cut his brother, Madly raged against his kindred,

scenes.title: Caused the blood to flow in streamlets
scenes.place: Caused the blood to flow in streamlets
scenes.reentry: From the wounds of man and hero. This, the origin of iron,

scenes.title: And of steel of light blue color.”
scenes.place: And of steel of light blue color.”
scenes.reentry: From the hearth arose the gray-beard,

scenes.title: Shook his heavy locks and answered:
scenes.place: Shook his heavy locks and answered:
scenes.reentry: “Now I know the source of iron, Whence the steel and whence its evils;

scenes.title: Curses on thee, cruel iron,
scenes.place: Curses on thee, cruel iron,
scenes.reentry: Curses on the steel thou givest, Curses on thee, tongue of evil,

scenes.title: Cursed be thy life forever!
scenes.place: Cursed be thy life forever!
scenes.reentry: Once thou wert of little value, Having neither form nor beauty,

scenes.title: Neither strength nor great importance,
scenes.place: Neither strength nor great importance,
scenes.reentry: When in form of milk thou rested, When for ages thou wert hidden

scenes.title: In the breasts of God’s three daughters,
scenes.place: In the breasts of God’s three daughters,
scenes.reentry: Hidden in their heaving bosoms, On the borders of the cloudlets,

scenes.title: In the blue vault of the heavens
scenes.place: In the blue vault of the heavens
scenes.reentry: “Thou wert once of little value,

scenes.title: Having neither form nor beauty,
scenes.place: Having neither form nor beauty,
scenes.reentry: Neither strength nor great importance, When like water thou wert resting

scenes.title: On the broad back of the marshes,
scenes.place: On the broad back of the marshes,
scenes.reentry: On the steep declines of mountains, When thou wert but formless matter,

scenes.title: Only dust of rusty color
scenes.place: Only dust of rusty color
scenes.reentry: “Surely thou wert void of greatness,

scenes.title: Having neither strength nor beauty,
scenes.place: Having neither strength nor beauty,
scenes.reentry: When the moose was trampling on thee, When the roebuck trod upon thee,

scenes.title: When the tracks of wolves were in thee,
scenes.place: When the tracks of wolves were in thee,
scenes.reentry: And the bear-paws scratched thy body. Surely thou hadst little value

scenes.title: When the skilful Ilmarinen,
scenes.place: When the skilful Ilmarinen,
scenes.reentry: First of all the iron-workers, Brought thee from the blackened swamp-lands,

scenes.title: Took thee to his ancient smithy,
scenes.place: Took thee to his ancient smithy,
scenes.reentry: Placed thee in his fiery furnace. Truly thou hadst little vigor,

scenes.title: Little strength, and little danger,
scenes.place: Little strength, and little danger,
scenes.reentry: When thou in the fire wert hissing, Rolling forth like seething water,

scenes.title: From the furnace of the smithy,
scenes.place: From the furnace of the smithy,
scenes.reentry: When thou gavest oath the strongest, By the furnace, by the anvil,

scenes.title: By the tongs, and by the hammer,
scenes.place: By the tongs, and by the hammer,
scenes.reentry: By the dwelling of the blacksmith, By the fire within the furnace.

scenes.title: Thou canst rage in wildest fury;
scenes.place: Thou canst rage in wildest fury;
scenes.reentry: Thou hast broken all thy pledges, All thy solemn vows hast broken,

scenes.title: Like the dogs thou shamest honor,
scenes.place: Like the dogs thou shamest honor,
scenes.reentry: Shamest both thyself and kindred, Tainted all with breath of evil.

scenes.title: Tell who drove thee to this mischief,
scenes.place: Tell who drove thee to this mischief,
scenes.reentry: Tell who taught thee all thy malice, Tell who gavest thee thine evil!

scenes.title: Did thy father, or thy mother,
scenes.place: Did thy father, or thy mother,
scenes.reentry: Did the eldest of thy brothers, Did the youngest of thy sisters,

scenes.title: Did the worst of all thy kindred
scenes.place: Did the worst of all thy kindred
scenes.reentry: Give to thee thine evil nature? Not thy father, nor thy mother,

scenes.title: Not the eldest of thy brothers,
scenes.place: Not the eldest of thy brothers,
scenes.reentry: Not the youngest of thy sisters, Not the worst of all thy kindred,

scenes.title: But thyself hast done this mischief,
scenes.place: But thyself hast done this mischief,
scenes.reentry: Thou the cause of all our trouble. Come and view thine evil doings,

scenes.title: And amend this flood of damage,
scenes.place: And amend this flood of damage,
scenes.reentry: Ere I tell thy gray-haired mother, Ere I tell thine aged father.

scenes.title: Great indeed a mother’s anguish,
scenes.place: Great indeed a mother’s anguish,
scenes.reentry: Great indeed a father’s sorrow, When a son does something evil,

scenes.title: When a child runs wild and lawless
scenes.place: When a child runs wild and lawless
scenes.reentry: “Crimson streamlet, cease thy flowing

scenes.title: From the wounds of Wainamoinen;
scenes.place: From the wounds of Wainamoinen;
scenes.reentry: Blood of ages, stop thy coursing From the veins of the magician;

scenes.title: Stand like heaven’s crystal pillars,
scenes.place: Stand like heaven’s crystal pillars,
scenes.reentry: Stand like columns in the ocean, Stand like birch-trees in the forest,

scenes.title: Like the tall reeds in the marshes,
scenes.place: Like the tall reeds in the marshes,
scenes.reentry: Like the high-rocks on the sea-coast, Stand by power of mighty magic!

scenes.title: Flow thou on thine endless circuit,
scenes.place: Flow thou on thine endless circuit,
scenes.reentry: Through the veins of Wainamoinen, Through the bones, and through the muscles,

scenes.title: Through the lungs, and heart, and liver,
scenes.place: Through the lungs, and heart, and liver,
scenes.reentry: Of the mighty sage and singer; Better be the food of heroes,

scenes.title: Than to waste thy strength and virtue,
scenes.place: Than to waste thy strength and virtue,
scenes.reentry: On the meadows and the woodlands, And be lost in dust and ashes.

scenes.title: Flow forever in thy circle;
scenes.place: Flow forever in thy circle;
scenes.reentry: Thou must cease this crimson out-flow; Stain no more the grass and flowers,

scenes.title: Stain no more these golden hill-tops,
scenes.place: Stain no more these golden hill-tops,
scenes.reentry: Pride and beauty of our heroes. In the veins of the magician,

scenes.title: In the heart of Wainamoinen,
scenes.place: In the heart of Wainamoinen,
scenes.reentry: Is thy rightful home and storehouse. Thither now withdraw thy forces,

scenes.title: Thither hasten, swiftly flowing;
scenes.place: Thither hasten, swiftly flowing;
scenes.reentry: Flow no more as crimson currents, Fill no longer crimson lakelets,

scenes.title: Must not rush like brooks in spring-tide,
scenes.place: Must not rush like brooks in spring-tide,
scenes.reentry: Nor meander like the rivers.

scenes.title: Cease as did the falls of Tyrya,
scenes.place: Cease as did the falls of Tyrya,
scenes.reentry: As the rivers of Tuoni, When the sky withheld her rain-drops,

scenes.title: When the sea gave up her waters,
scenes.place: When the sea gave up her waters,
scenes.reentry: In the famine of the seasons, In the years of fire and torture.

scenes.title: If thou heedest not this order,
scenes.place: If thou heedest not this order,
scenes.reentry: I shall offer other measures, Know I well of other forces;

scenes.title: I shall call the Hisi irons,
scenes.place: I shall call the Hisi irons,
scenes.reentry: In them I shall boil and roast thee, Thus to check thy crimson flowing,

scenes.title: Thus to save the wounded hero
scenes.place: Thus to save the wounded hero
scenes.reentry: “If these means be inefficient,

scenes.title: Should these measures prove unworthy,
scenes.place: Should these measures prove unworthy,
scenes.reentry: I shall call omniscient Ukko, Mightiest of the creators,

scenes.title: Stronger than all ancient heroes,
scenes.place: Stronger than all ancient heroes,
scenes.reentry: Wiser than the world-magicians; He will check the crimson out-flow,

scenes.title: He will heal this wound of hatchet
scenes.place: He will heal this wound of hatchet
scenes.reentry: “Ukko, God of love and mercy,

scenes.title: God and Master of the heavens,
scenes.place: God and Master of the heavens,
scenes.reentry: Come thou hither, thou art needed, Come thou quickly I beseech thee,

scenes.title: Lend thy hand to aid thy children,
scenes.place: Lend thy hand to aid thy children,
scenes.reentry: Touch this wound with healing fingers, Stop this hero’s streaming life-blood,

scenes.title: Bind this wound with tender leaflets,
scenes.place: Bind this wound with tender leaflets,
scenes.reentry: Mingle with them healing flowers, Thus to check this crimson current,

scenes.title: Thus to save this great magician,
scenes.place: Thus to save this great magician,
scenes.reentry: Save the life of Wainamoinen.”

scenes.title: Thus at last the blood-stream ended,
scenes.place: Thus at last the blood-stream ended,
scenes.reentry: As the magic words were spoken. Then the gray-beard, much rejoicing,

scenes.title: Sent his young son to the smithy,
scenes.place: Sent his young son to the smithy,
scenes.reentry: There to make a healing balsam, From the herbs of tender fibre,

scenes.title: From the healing plants and flowers,
scenes.place: From the healing plants and flowers,
scenes.reentry: From the stalks secreting honey, From the roots, and leaves, and blossoms.

scenes.title: On the way he meets an oak-tree,
scenes.place: On the way he meets an oak-tree,
scenes.reentry: And the oak the son addresses: “Hast thou honey in thy branches,

scenes.title: Does thy sap run full of sweetness?”
scenes.place: Does thy sap run full of sweetness?”
scenes.reentry: Thus the oak-tree wisely answers: “Yea, but last night dripped the honey

scenes.title: Down upon my spreading branches,
scenes.place: Down upon my spreading branches,
scenes.reentry: And the clouds their fragrance sifted, Sifted honey on my leaflets,

scenes.title: From their home within the heavens.”
scenes.place: From their home within the heavens.”
scenes.reentry: Then the son takes oak-wood splinters,

scenes.title: Takes the youngest oak-tree branches,
scenes.place: Takes the youngest oak-tree branches,
scenes.reentry: Gathers many healing grasses, Gathers many herbs and flowers,

scenes.title: Rarest herbs that grow in Northland,
scenes.place: Rarest herbs that grow in Northland,
scenes.reentry: Places them within the furnace In a kettle made of copper;

scenes.title: Lets them steep and boil together,
scenes.place: Lets them steep and boil together,
scenes.reentry: Bits of bark chipped from the oak-tree, Many herbs of healing virtues;

scenes.title: Steeps them one day, then a second,
scenes.place: Steeps them one day, then a second,
scenes.reentry: Three long days of summer weather, Days and nights in quick succession;

scenes.title: Then he tries his magic balsam,
scenes.place: Then he tries his magic balsam,
scenes.reentry: Looks to see if it is ready, If his remedy is finished;

scenes.title: But the balsam is unworthy
scenes.place: But the balsam is unworthy
scenes.reentry: Then he added other grasses,

scenes.title: Herbs of every healing virtue,
scenes.place: Herbs of every healing virtue,
scenes.reentry: That were brought from distant nations, Many hundred leagues from Northland,

scenes.title: Gathered by the wisest minstrels,
scenes.place: Gathered by the wisest minstrels,
scenes.reentry: Thither brought by nine enchanters. Three days more he steeped the balsam,

scenes.title: Three nights more the fire he tended,
scenes.place: Three nights more the fire he tended,
scenes.reentry: Nine the days and nights he watched it, Then again he tried the ointment,

scenes.title: Viewed it carefully and tested,

scenes.reentry: Found at last that it was ready, Found the magic balm was finished.

scenes.title: Near by stood a branching birch-tree,
scenes.place: Near by stood a branching birch-tree,
scenes.reentry: On the border of the meadow, Wickedly it had been broken,

scenes.title: Broken down by evil Hisi;
scenes.place: Broken down by evil Hisi;

scenes.title: Rubs the balsam in the fractures,
scenes.place: Rubs the balsam in the fractures,
